Le concept est efficace et propre, les mécaniques arrivent petit à petit afin que le joueur comprenne ce qu'il fait au fil des premières parties.
L'histoire est relativement classique mais le gameplay brodé autour est plutôt original et intéressant.
Je ne suis pas un grand adepte de city builder, mais la formule fonctionne ici justement car ce n'est pas un simple city builder : chaque nouvelle colonie présente son lot de difficulté, modulé par les ressources disponibles, les caravanes de colons que l'on peut envoyer, et ainsi de suite.

Maintenant, si l'évolution de début de partie est intéressante et engageante, le jeu perds malheureusement en intérêt sur la durée, car tout est beaucoup trop long et lent, et après 63h j'ai l'impression de n'avoir pas accompli le quart de tout ce qu'il y a à faire.
Pire que ça, après plusieurs heures passées sur une partie, je perds ma run sur une génération de quêtes obligatoire pour gagner qui m'est juste impossible à accomplir. 
J'en suis déjà à un cap ou j'ai l'impression de progresser beaucoup trop lentement dans le jeu et voilà que ma run de plusieurs heures se voit écourtée sans recours possible par de l'aléatoire, le problème n'est même pas la difficulté car le jeu reste assez détendu et facile d'accès initialement.

Mettre des mécaniques aussi punitives au sein d'un jeu dont la progression est beaucoup trop lente, ça refroidit sévère, et c'est vraiment dommage parce que le concept de base est très efficace et divertissant.

Je m'en tiendrai à ça personnellement, j'ai apprécié l'expérience jusque là mais je n'ai plus aucune envie d'y mettre du temps actuellement.
C'est un bon jeu mais c'est aussi un jeu qui en demande trop pour ce qu'il est, l'aventure détendue du début paraît bien trop loin malheureusement.

Cet avis reste une recommandation car j'ai quand même apprécié l'expérience jusque là, le concept est assez original et répondre aux défis assez spécifiques de chaque colonie est intéressant.

У игры нет явной концовки, а предложенная прогрессия требует сотен часов — но взамен часто предлагает какие-то процентные пункты (!) к продуктивности в качестве «прокачки».
Каждый раз ты будешь обнаруживать себя на пятачке земли, расставлять пять одних и тех же зданий, чертить дороги по всё той же привычной схеме; и ждать, пока дровосеки расчистят столь важное пространство, прорубят путь к опушкам с новыми ресурсами и задачами.
К тому же, зданий и рецептов не то, чтобы много — большинство сорокаминутных экспедиций будет сводиться к решению уже ранее решённых задач, просто со слегка другими вводными и переменными, но без особого разнообразия.

[h2]女王的恩情還不完--《風暴之城Against the Storm》14個小時個人遊玩感想[/h2]

筆者在14個小時的遊玩後，終於完成本遊戲的所有教程。而後續本遊戲並無提供具體的遊玩目標。因此，筆者覺得這款《風暴之城 Against the Storm》的遊玩體驗可以告一個段落，並給出親身遊玩後的感想了。

首先，請原諒筆者偷懶，具體的玩法煩請諸位查看上面的官方的PV。個人認為PV展現的非常清楚。

本作實際上的分類應該是模擬城市建設類，只不過進行了現代化的改造以及增添了肉鴿（Rouge-like）“風味”：
①本作隨時可以暫停，並在UI界面頂部提供了最高可達3倍速的高速模式以供玩家自行選擇。為此可以更快地度過那些無聊的等待原材料開採/物資生產的“垃圾”時間；
②每一局的遊戲時長控制在45分鐘到1小時內，不至於讓玩家感到過於冗長；加上背景音樂OST是能烘托季節氛圍的，因此單一局的遊玩體驗會比較舒適。
③絕大部分關卡有明確的過關目標：在UI界面底部紅條（女皇的急躁值）滿前，先填滿藍條（女皇的滿意度）即可；④女皇在遊戲過程中會分發任務，完成任務後女皇會給予玩家城鎮建築藍圖獎勵（基礎建築藍圖自帶，但高級/稀有的藍圖得在遊玩中抽取，因此每局遊玩體驗各不相同），而且都是多選一，當然重選/放棄的機會也不會“缺席”。
⑤本作中，絕大部分生產建築可以隨時移動位置（因為資源會隨開採枯竭），移動不了的建築也能無損拆除（返還建造資源）。移動生成建築的時候，遊戲會及時顯示已探明的建築對應的可開採資源的圖標，方便玩家順利地移動建築到指定地點。點擊任意資源，均可查看所需的生產建築。
⑥除了伐木場需要指定砍伐位置外，其餘生產建築都是派遣人員後自動運行的。而生產物資所需的物料都有複數的原材料可以供指定，因此不至於產生任務進度完全卡住的狀況。
⑦有局外天賦樹，可以用每局遊戲通關後獲得的代幣“點亮”，能夠提供額外的便利性。例如開局多攜帶資源，資源存儲量上升，人員滿意度上升等諸如此類的加成。

本遊戲的缺點自然也是有的：
①首當其衝，就是重複作業感。雖然每局任務/獲取的藍圖各不相同，但大部分的遊玩體驗還是極其相似的，不外乎就是開採資源，生產物資，開拓空地，解決這些空地上的威脅並滿足女皇而已。所以，對筆者這種模擬城市建設小白來說，玩一遍覺得新鮮，5遍覺得有點膩，10遍開始就是機械作業了……_(:з」∠)_
②新手引導還是有瑕疵，不夠完善。筆者就遇到過“需要造木材加工廠來生產木板，但木材加工廠本身的建立需要木板”的窘境。而實際上獲取木板的方法還有通過“臨時工作站”加工和“商棧”交易獲得。諸如此類的這些東西都是需要玩家自己去一點一點熟悉、摸索本遊戲後才會清楚的。
③建築繁多，但單個辨識度有點低。雖然當原材料開採殆盡後，左下角會彈出提示，點擊此提示會跳轉到對應建築物。但平時，想要查看個別建築時（特別是後期扎堆造了一堆建築時），那真的是眼花繚亂的頭疼。
④應該是模擬城市建設的通病吧：“刁民”們，是真的有點難伺候。從一開始的吃飽，到穿好，再到工作安排到位，後期還有教育、祭祀、鬥毆等一系列進階要求。不滿足，他們就會滿意度下降，甚至直接“罷工跑路”。筆者就經常在每局遊戲的中後期被這些要求搞的焦頭爛額……

以上，就是筆者親身遊玩《風暴之城 Against the Storm》14個小時後的一些淺薄的感想。本人畢竟只是這類遊戲的入門小白，上面的信息肯定會有錯漏，煩請有玩過的諸位補充糾正，感激不盡。 總體來說，《風暴之城 Against the Storm》的遊戲質量對的起它在steam商店的“壓倒性好評”的評價。但如果你不是此類模擬城市建設遊戲的愛好者，那還是建議謹慎購買，多看看YT上實際的遊戲遊玩實況後再做決定；以免衝著折扣和高評價而衝動消費後，卻收穫"買了後悔而壓倉底"的糟糕體驗。

Absolutely wonderful game! Such an immersive art style and OST, up to the point that I sometimes get stuck in the main menu for a few minutes just chilling with nice music and rain sounds. 

Your goal is to build settlements on your way to reforge seals. Each settlement will take you 1-4 hours depending on several factors, with how well you know the game being the most important one.

The settlement gameplay is a mix of production management, colony survival and a bit of city building, thoroughly spiced with rogue-lite elements and RNG. You will have to plan a lot and make use of what you have to please your citizens and get enough reputation points, otherwise you will loose the settlement (more about the clock below). You will also have to learn to quickly adapt, because RNG is all over the game, and you never know whether the next glade will be your doom or your blessing.

There seems to be a common confusion about the city building aspect. It is there, but it barely the point of the game. While you do build cities, your main focus is to survive until you get enough reputation points to move on to the next one. In each settlement there will be a clock in form of Queen's impatience, up on reaching which you lose the current settlement (no casualties applied, you only lose time in the current cycle), so there isn't much time for chill city building (at least not on higher difficulties).

If all this sounds like a game you would play, and you find the art style and the whole rainpunk theme appealing, then I definitely recommend getting the game. It is truly a gem. With its nearly endless replayability, it can bring you a lot of hours of play time.

Переосмысление жанра: градостроительный рогалик здорового человека

Разработчикам из Eremite Games удалось решить главную проблему классических градосимуляторов. Обычно в таких играх самое интересное происходит в первые часы, когда идет борьба за выживание, а финал превращается в ленивое созерцание работающего конвейера. Against the Storm забирает этот сочный начальный этап, превращает его в сессию на 40-60 минут и заставляет играть по законам рогалика.

Игровой цикл: баланс между нетерпением и репутацией
Вы выступаете в роли Наместника Тлеющего Города. Ваша задача - отправляться в неизведанные леса, строить небольшие поселения и собирать ресурсы для Королевы до того, как мир накроет очередной Гнилостный Шторм.

Вместо бесконечного расширения здесь есть четкие условия победы и поражения, отображаемые двумя шкалами:
Репутация (синяя полоса) - заполняется за счет выполнения приказов и высокого настроения жителей. Полная шкала означает успешное завершение миссии.
Нетерпение (красная полоса) - увеличивается каждую минуту, а также при гибели поселенцев. Если она заполнится, вас отзывают, а миссия считается проваленной.

Этот механизм формирует постоянное напряжение. Игра не дает расслабиться. Вы постоянно ищете компромиссы: выполнить сложный приказ прямо сейчас или потратить ресурсы на стабилизацию лагеря.

Управление видами и психология выживания
Основа микроменеджмента - работа с населением, состоящим из разных фэнтезийных рас. В одном забеге вам могут достаться люди, бобры и ящеры, а в следующем - гарпии и лисы. Каждая раса обладает своими чертами, предпочтениями в еде, жилье и работе:

Бобры - отличные инженеры и дровосеки, обожают деревянные дома.
Ящеры - любят тепло, профессионально работают с мясом и требуют внимания к традициям.
Гарпии - хрупкие, но крайне полезные в производстве тканей и алхимии.

Удержать баланс сложно. Если решимость расы падает ниже нуля, жители начинают уходить, что поднимает шкалу нетерпения Королевы. Наоборот, если вы обеспечите их пирогами, хорошей одеждой и услугами в таверне, они начнут приносить очки репутации. Это заставляет выстраивать производственные линии не ради абстрактной прибыли, а ради конкретных потребностей ваших подданных прямо сейчас.

Враждебность леса и сезонность
Мир игры живет в трех сезонах: Капель (время созидания), Просвет (сбор урожая) и Буря. Буря - это местный экзамен на прочность. В это время включаются сильные негативные эффекты, зависящие от общего уровня Враждебности леса.

Враждебность увеличивается от количества лет, проведенных на карте, и от открытых просек (глейдов). Просеки бывают мелкими и опасными. Открывая опасную просеку, вы получаете много ресурсов, но вместе с ними и случайное событие: древнее проклятие, утечку скверны или логово монстра. Вам дается несколько минут на то, чтобы отправить рабочих со специфическими материалами на ликвидацию угрозы. Ошиблись со временем - половина лагеря погибнет во время Бури.

Ближе к финалу глобальной карты, когда вы открываете уровни Престижа, игра превращается в строгую математическую задачу. Одна случайная ошибка с выбором чертежей на старте может сделать забег почти непроходимым. Иногда рандом бывает излишне суров, заставляя собирать сложные цепи без ключевых построек, например, мельницы или пекарни.

Тем не менее, Against the Storm - это выдающийся триумф инди-дизайна. Она собирает лучшее от двух жанров и заставляет серое вещество работать на полную мощность, при этом бережно относясь к времени игрока. Один из лучших тактических симуляторов последних лет.

One of my favorite games! Instead of applauding the game, I would like to answer some recent criticism that I found in negative reviews. 

1. The game always have a win condition. Some people say that it might be impossible to fulfill the orders, but YOU DON'T NEED the orders to win the game. In one scenario you don't receive any orders (1) at all, and you have to win by gaining points through opening dangerous glades (2) or resolve (3). You win a typical party by a combination of orders (1), glades (2), and resolve (3). People who complain about impossible orders don't understand the game mechanics. 

2. Difficulty. The game has increasing levels of difficulty. It has a learning curve, so you SHOULD BEGIN ON EASY MODE, instead of higher difficulties. Because it's a rouge-lite with meta-progession, you WILL be getting more updates and improvements, as well as you will be understanding the systems better. Some people think that they are to hard-core to be playing on easy mode (without any upgrades), and they blame the game for being difficult. That's insane. The game is easy and very forgiving on easy mode and you have to go to the 3rd or 4th level of difficulty to really feel the hostility of the forest.

3. The gameplay loop. The game is about creating new settlements, which should take you around 60-120 to set-up. You're struggling with insufficient resources, lacking production-chains, you need to discover and adapt. It's fun. When you win, YOU CAN CONTINUE playing with your settlement, but it's not fun, because everything is optimized and autonomous. But you can stay and watch how the villagers take care of everything. 

4. I DON'T KNOW WHICH BUILDING TO CHOOSE ;-; That is the point of this game. You have to understand the production chains. Each building has different efficiency, e.g. planks can be produces with 1 star efficiency or 3 stars. It means that you need, let's say, 8 wood to produce 1 plank or 4 wood to produce a plank. So you have to know the supply chains and resources that are on the map and make decisions accordingly. Do I want to choose a building that increases the efficiency of plank production given that we have not enough wood (in some forests), do I want to produce planks (I can buy them from a merchant and produce sth else), or do I maybe need a plantation, so that my villagers don't starve? Do I want to optimize the efficiency of one supply-chain or am I happy with mediocre optimization and I want to be able to produce more food, because I really need it. (I can have fewer villagers, so food might not be that urgent). 

5. Every party is similar. No it's not. It's like saying that every game of chess or every piano piece is the same. IF you're new it might well be, but the tiny differences make for HUGE VARIANCE in the gameplay. At a first glance it might look similar, but if you've reached the skill ceiling, it's like night and day. 

6. The game is too complicated. No it's not. IT'S INGENIOUS how good it is. It's not an excel sheet, but it's so unbelievably well optimized. You have to control minimum and maximum supply in your magasins, you have to control which resources can be use (AND CANNOT!!!) be used as substitutes (that is extremely important) in your production chains, you have to control which race is in charge of which production facilities. But there is a handy shortcut for everything, it doesn't play like an excel sheet. That is the single most impressive thing: the intuitive, user friendly UI that allows you to control the complex systems in the game, that you should be discovering and mastering during your first 20 hours. 

So if you buy this game, start with 3rd level of difficulty (because you're not a noob...), you're gonna be overwhelmed. If you give it some time, it will be one of the most fulfilling experiences.

Hello Interested consumer,
I've been looking at playing this game for a couple years and bought it on sale. So far I've enjoyed it a lot.
Pros:
-Relatively easy to learn, but new mechanics are introduced that make gameplay more engaging as you master it.
-Fast pace means that you can be satisfied with sessions of 30 to 40 minutes.
-Sound effects, music, and artwork give strong ambience of melancholy and relaxedness.
-Interesting lore influenced by Wheel of Time, Lovecraft, and other fantasy works.
Negatives:
- Personally, I enjoy video games with a strong narrative focus. This game has no cutscenes or linear storyline with characters. Instead, the lore is mostly window-dressing for the gameplay. This means that I was less emotionally invested in the gameplay.
Positive/Negative:
-The rogue-lite structure of the game means that every settlement has different resources, strategies, and challenges, which makes gameplay very adaptive and engaging. However, the impermanence of settlements leads to a lack of meaning and investment in individual settlements.
My score: 8/10
Would definitely recommend on-sale, especially for people who play video games primarily for the mechanical aspect of video games. Less so for people who are more focused on story or aesthetics.

I'm having a hard time with this one. It scratches a lot of that old Warcraft/Starcraft itch, especially when compared to their mods, but there's just something missing. It gets called a city builder a lot, but I would hard disagree with that descriptor. You have to expand, and I found myself constantly moving buildings around. You're not building a "city" out of interest, you're doing it out of economic necessity. This is doubly true with how the progression works in this game and with how you're handed choices against your own opinion. Unfortunately, the game just feels like it's more resource manager than anything else. That includes how you handle the events themselves, though it sprinkles in RNG elements to keep it somewhat dynamic. On the other hand, it's (at least on lower difficulties) surprisingly calming and enjoyable enough to keep me desiring of more. There appears to be a handful of different ways to approach every scenario, and I do feel like there are clever approaches here that allow it to pigeon hole itself as a pacifist Age of Mythology. However, I never felt like I could approach scenarios with a game-plan in hand or with prechosen perks to get a unique identity off the ground. It almost forces you to play by its rules, and I'm just not that kind of person especially with this genre. I don't get it. It's better than not, and I think there's a lot of choice provided here even if half of it is a fugazi. This is a game for a very specific type of person without a lot of time on their hands: old heads that min/maxed Civ or games like Dungeons III.

I really enjoyed it. I've tried other city-builders before but this is the first time something stuck with me. And as I learned the game after several cycles, I continued improving and optimizing my cities throughout the cycles. 

I saw on some other reviews that the game eventually becomes a pause/play, rinse and repeat play, which is fair criticism. But personally, I think that's one of the appeal the game has.

Once I learned the mechanics, there was just this feeling in me that I want to optimize my woodcutters, so I build warehouses near them. I want all of my workers to be doing something, whether production/harvest/gather, etc but not leave them be. I want them to only reach a certain resource amount before I re-assigned them to different things. So it does becomes a pause-play and watch your optimization goes well.

Maximizing the reputation eventually becomes easy and having a selectable difficulty per city, which let me learn and adapt to the game mechanics fast enough. 

There were dangerous glade events which affects your cities, but I honestly didn't feel the impact that much until I played in the Veteran difficulty. After a few cycles, Pioneer difficulty became easier to accomplish and a bit dull so ramping up the difficulty by one makes the experience different.

Rainpunk, Corruption and Blightrot gets introduced and from there, on top of Hostility, resource management, timing glade events with limited people, RNG, you also have to deal with another mechanic that influences your city.

I can handle Veteran stages but upping the difficulty further to just Viceroy is too hard for me. I'm sure others can handle it better than I do, but even if I didn't reach the highest difficulty, I'm satisfied with the game.

Overall, I liked that core idea is that the cities are not forever, there's a goal to achieve, and I also realized here why I don't like open-sandbox games without any goals, I like my games to eventually end. So the game at most can be played in an hour or less at lower difficulties and around 2 hours or so on higher ones.

Perhaps that why this one stuck the most to me. I don't have to maintain it forever.

On a side note, before I adapted on how to manage needs of the people, I really hated Harpies the most. They're the ones who really like to leave my cities with their annoying low resolve. Just 1 Hostility level then they're already in the negatives, seriously?

TLDR: Game's replay value is great, its mechanics are easy to learn, optimizing it is fun, and you can accomplish a city 1-2 hours.

You’re always leveling your account, unlocking things for future runs, and building toward larger goals. Some settlements even connect together, which makes the world feel alive instead of isolated matches.

The tutorial was also done really well. It explained the systems without dragging on, and I was able to pick things up naturally while playing.

What I really like is that failure still feels rewarding. Even if a settlement falls apart, you still gain experience and resources for future runs. It never feels like wasted time.

There’s also a lot more depth here than I expected. The game constantly pushes you to adapt, and figuring things out feels rewarding instead of frustrating.

Performance has been great too. I’m playing on a Zephyrus G14 laptop and the game runs smoothly without issues.

It’s one of the few city builders that keeps me interested after a settlement is finished.

This is a genuine gem of a game. 

At it's core the gameplay is the early parts of a city builder. Then once you get into the repetative I've won this settlement and am just taking it easy phase, you get to confirm the win, buy a few city upgrades, and start the challenging and fun part again in a new settlement with a different set of conditions. Each settlement builds on a world map that comes with it's own challenges and rewards and then gets reset every storm cycle. (after X years) But this summary doesn't really do the game justice... 

It's exceptionally replayable. You may have a solid run of games, then put it down for a few months, then feel like it again and come back for another few weeks. Each time you do so the gradual progression of the game becomes more apparent. It's hit the sweet spot for challenge and reward. Yes, if you want you can just cruise along on the lower difficulties and enjoy a relaxing build, but you can also start aiming to build your citys out towards boss map type "seals" in cursed forests. If you manage to meet the requirements and beat a seal the storm cycle gets a bit longer and theres a new higher level seal you can aim for. Getting to the later seals comes with increasing minimum difficultly levels on the map the further you get from the start and these can become very difficult. So difficult, that achieving them brings genuine tension to the playthrough and genuinely feels rewarding once achieved. 

One of the things that keeps the game interesting is that the 'between city upgrades' change the style of how you achieve victory over time. So the path to victory utilised early in the game for low difficulty wouldn't be enough for the high difficulty games where you need more victory pointy and you have to adapt your thinking on the fly to eak out a victory by exploiting the right things at the right time. And the game would be great if it stopped there. 

Where it overachieves is the addition of the queens had trial which requires a very nuanced understanding of the game to achieve. Once you forge the adamantine seal it's pretty impressive as that's the highest seal of the main game. This unlocks the trial. The trial is a permadeath mode that sets you back to the beginning for upgrades and you need to forge a seal way out on the highest difficulty with a different way of getting upgrades on the main map as you go. This forces you to employ game tactics you haven't used since early game right through to the late game tactics in a single storm cycle. The subtlty required to create this as an achievable yet fairly (as in not overly RNG) difficult challenge is impressive.

AtS is an RTS game with rouge lite components and a city-builder presentation.  

You (as an abstract character) are tasked with developing a series of settlements within a given “cycle”. A settlement is developed through the construction of a series of buildings and natural resource collecting nodes defining a series of production chains, with the ultimate deliverables being a variety of the products of these various chains. If you deliver enough of the required goods, and generally complete enough of the required tasks, in a short enough period of time, then the settlement is considered a success. With enough successfully completed settlements constructed within a cycle, you will have the opportunity to “close a seal”, with one of the primary goals of the entire game being to complete said seals. 

Each successful settlement earns you some meta-progress in terms of resource production, starting equipment, buildings available and so forth, as part of a very impressive progression tree. After enough settlement attempts have been made (successful or not) the cycle will end, and you will start from scratch in your effort to close the next seals on the list (while obviously retaining your meta-progression).

Pros:
+++ The RTS gameplay is quite challenging (especially at higher difficulty levels) but is typically quite doable and very satisfying in victory.
+++ The randomness present adds enormous replayability to each settlement attempt, in terms of items available, blueprints available (i.e. which buildings you are allowed to build), the goals you must achieve, the biomes you are playing in (which differ in some rules as well natural resource availability), the races you are offered and so forth.
++ The meta-progression is very well done.
++ The UI is quite serviceable for navigating the demands of the game.
+ Difficulty scaling is OK, noting that I stopped playing at Prestige 10.
+ Very reasonably priced on sale.

Cons:
-- I really disliked the “close the seal” settlement missions. I found the extra requirements somewhat unfun and the maps quite lengthy.

 Summary: AtS is just a brilliantly constructed RTS experience. In particular, the elegance of the combined systems in conjunction with the replayability introduced through the game’s run-to-run randomness make for a highly addictive experience. Unfortunately (for me), I found seal -closing tedious and after I closed the first four seals, the prospect of making it through the remaining seals (combined with my already substantial playtime) removed my desire for future runs. Still, I got more than my money’s worth out of this unique gaming experience and this game is easy to recommend to fans of the RTS, city-building/production-chain genre.

Overall: 9.0/10

Pretty much the quintessential roguelike city builder.
You are in charge of a settlement. The goal is to gain enough victory (reputation) points fast enough so that you outpace the constantly growing impatience bar.
You lose if impatience reaches max.
You win if the reputation reaches max.
The simplicity of the premise allows for the actual gameplay to be as complex as you want it to be.
You might choose to make your villagers as happy as possible, you can try to tackle the tasks that give reputation points or you can venture out into the forest to tackle high-risk high-reward events.
Just watch out for the storm!

Against the Storm isn't just a game you play; it’s a game you keep. It is the gold standard for how to respect a player's time while providing infinite replayability. If you want a strategy game that stays fresh even after months of neglect, this is it.

This game has really surprised me, it's much better than I had anticipated. even if the formula is extremely weird and it has to be said that the "Tutorial phase" is extremely long. 

So Whats so cool about AtS? Its just a great take on the citybuilder genre. While most citybuilders have dozens of maps and maybe some production goals and building restrictions that keep the player interested. But lets be honest, usually you play along for a while and then just build the biggest most awesome megacity with all the stuffs at that point there is little point to continue. 

Now AtS forgoes that. There are some special missions but usually you just need to get your score to the target value, however you see fit. Apart fromt the "earlygame"(which is quite long) things are not locked in the traditional sense. And the maps are all flat forests, where you cut yourself through to find glades with events and resources. But that sort of the clue. Every map you start with a different three species of settlers that all have different needs and different bonuses. each map is different because the glades are randomized in terms of events and res. So you never know what you will have to work with and what you needs do you need to fill. Then you start with some basic buildings unlocked but every map you need to unlock the other buildings, which you can do based on chance. so one game you might get the farm in your opening hand and others you might never see it. Then you get Missions and bonuses(like get one X everytime you get Y) in a similar manner. You usually pick one out of 2-4 of these so you have some control. but in general you need to adapt to what you have to work with. this works because the Production recipes mostly have alternative ingredients. For example you might want to produce foodpase which your harpies crave. you can produce those from the basic kitchen 1:1 or you might have the cannery unlocked which can produce at 3:5, it can also produce biscuits and wine which your harpies do not care about but your beavers are great fans of. Either way the recipe calls for Dye and Eggs, but if you dont produce those, you might want to use Salt instead of dye and Fish or meat instead of Eggs. I try not to think about what exactly it is they eat. So every game you need to customize your build to the conditions, go for different objectives and utilize different chains. 

on top of that there are random map modifiers, that stack on top of that, and further inform what you can let slide and where you have to be vigilant. 

So every game is unique in significant ways. That's all nice and good but im not done yet. Another thing I really enjoy is how the game entices you to increace the difficulty. The further you want to go on the overland map the higher the minimum difficulty. So if you want to do the Golden seal you need to play on Viceroy or higher. It's a good way to push yourself in a fairly relaxed genre. There is far more here with rainpunk, forest hostility and my favorite mechanic, stacking bonuses.
It's good, cleared a gold seal, but I can't really bring myself to do the higher prestiges and seals of this game, feels a bit samey. It was a fun 60 hours though

Postanowiłem ostatnio napisać kilka recenzji tych gier, które na to zasługują, a które mam od dawna w bibliotece. Uznałem, że chcę mieć swój (zapewne nieduży, ale jednak) wkład w "dobry, ambitny gaming". A nie będzie on dobry, jeśli oryginalne tytuły nie będą doceniane, a cały szum i uwaga będą wyłącznie wokół tytułów AAA. To powiedziawszy, zabieram się do roboty.
Pierwszą grą na liście okazała się "Against the Storm". Tytuł, który początkowo ogrywałem na steam decku a z czasem przeniosłem się na większy ekran. A że stuknęło mi w nim 200+ godzin, uznałem, że gierka na recenzję zasłużyła.

O czym jest ta gra?

W skrócie: 
To troszkę taka strategia ekonomiczna, w której tworząc łańcuchy dostaw zaspokajamy przeróżne potrzeby naszych mieszkańców oraz walczymy z wszelakiej maści przeciwnościami losu - z tytułową burzą na czele. 
Ale nie tylko - grę mocno przyprawiono elementami "rogue-lite" co samo w sobie stanowi bardzo interesującą i rzadko spotykaną mieszankę. Przez tę rogalikową przyprawę tytuł zyskuje sporą grywalność  (oraz regrywalność) pod warunkiem, że jesteś odbiorcą, który lubi tego typu formułę.

Troszkę dłużej:
To co widzisz na trailerach nie do końca ma odzwierciedlenie w rzeczywistości. Owszem, gra serwuje przyjemną dla oka i spójną grafikę (troszkę taki styl Warcraft 3) oraz klimatyczny soundtrack. Ale jeśli liczysz na jakieś epickie walki z bestiami, które widać na trailerach, to się pomyliłeś (ale nie znaczy to, że się zawiedziesz).
W grze nie ma czegoś takiego jak wojsko czy walka. Jest czysta ekonomia. Wszystko co budujesz i robisz czynisz po to, by uzyskać jakiś zasób, który z kolei możesz wykorzystać do produkcji innego zasobu czy też czyniąc z nim inne rzeczy. Te "inne rzeczy" są dosyć oryginalne - otwieramy skrzynie, spełniamy zadania na poszczególnych polanach, spełniamy wolę królowej, bawimy się w archeologa, płacimy za przetrwanie burzy, niszczymy zgniliznę pożerającą naszą osadę, czy też karmimy stworka w osadzie, który w zamian robi dla nas bardzo cenną kupkę :) Słowem - jest tu co robić.

Ekonomia to jedno, drugą sprawą są elementy rogue-lite, które w tej grze funkcjonują na bardzo wielu polach. Każda osada to zupełnie inna gra, a to za sprawą losowości. Losowe są budynki - więc nie zawsze zbudujesz tartak, by skorzystać z obfitości drewna. Mało tego - nie zawsze budynki układają się w "łańcuch" - czyli masz farmę (zboże), masz piekarnię (chleb czy inne placki) ale co z tego, jak nie masz młyna, więc ze zboża nie zrobisz mąki i nici z pieczywa. Co to oznacza? Że będziesz kombinował. Z każdą grą coraz bardziej i bardziej. Będziesz szukał wyjścia z sytuacji, w które wpuszcza Cię gra. Zwłaszcza, że każdą osadę można (a nieraz wręcz trzeba) wygrać nieco inaczej. Co zatem robimy z tym co mamy? Zboże sprzedajemy lub nastawiamy się na produkcję piwa. Piekarnię przestawiamy na produkcję zasobów, które da się ogarnąć bez mąki. I próbujemy pójść drogą inną, niż zakładaliśmy. Z tego powodu mocno nagradzana jest elastyczność myślenia i kreatywność.

Losowość- to jest element będący błogosławieństwem tej produkcji, ale zawiera też pewien mankament, o którym powiem później. Losowi są mieszkańcy Twojej osady - może zagrasz ludźmi i harpiami, które wiele różni, ale łączy zamiłowanie do ubrań, więc szyjąc ciuchy ułatwisz sobie grę. A może będą to lubiące przygody lisy, ciepłolubne jaszczury albo żaby, które w byle chatce nie będą chciały mieszkać. Każda osada to 3 losowe rasy spośród kilku. Do tego każda osada to inny biom. Od dosyć prostych zielonych lasów, po mokradła, gdzie trzeba wysyłać łazika po plany budynków. Są biomy obfitujące w jedzenie, biomy wymuszające górnictwo, ale też takie, gdzie nie ma np. drewna, bo wszystkie drzewa są z kamienia. 
Losowe są też poszczególne polany, przez które przebijamy się w lesie. Nigdy nie wiemy jakie zagrożenie na nas czeka, gdy wyrąbiemy sobie drogę przez las. Czasem jesteśmy na nie świetnie przygotowani i nas nie dotknie- a czasem wpadamy w głębokie szambo i walczymy o przetrwanie.
Losowość jest też w efektach "burzy", bo każda burza to inne zagrożenia, czasem proste, czasem nie. Nieraz te zagrożenia będą wymagały zupełnie innego podejścia do gry, niż sobie zaplanowaliśmy, bo np. może się okazać, że ścinając drzewa w burzy rozgniewamy las, albo bezdomni mieszkańcy będą porywani przez ciemność.
Wszystkie te losowe mechaniki są bardzo angażujące i ciekawe, a odkrywanie, co gra ma do zaoferowania zajmuje masę czasu i nie nudzi się szybko. Gra do pewnego momentu ma bardzo fajny poziom trudności, nieustannie stawiając przed nami wyzwania - ale bez frustrowania. 

Jednak przychodzi taki moment, gdy gra przestaje cieszyć jak na początku. U mnie to było po jakiś 100h gry, potem ten czas przedłużyły jeszcze dodatki.
Po pierwsze - dość wolny progres ulepszeń w cytadeli (to takie trwałe ulepszenia dla każdej nowej osady),  co powoduje, że musimy rozegrać kilka kolejnych (często podobnych) osad, by odblokować jakąś pierdołę typu lepsze domy dla lisów. Wg mnie pomysł z cytadelą dobry, ale z uwagi na wolny progres czuć trochę, że włożony wysiłek jest nieadekwatny do nagrody.
Po drugie - kolejne poziomy trudności (typu prestiż 5,6,7 itp) nie emocjonują już tak bardzo, jak te poprzednie, bo zamiast dodawać do gry ciekawe wyzwania zwykle dodają kolejną upierdliwość, o której trzeba pamiętać. Mi najfajniej gra się na poziomie Prestiż 1 lub 2, bo każdy kolejny rodzi więcej frustracji niż radochy. I tu trochę szkoda, że w kolejnych poziomach prestiżu trudność nie jest budowana stawianiem ciekawych wyzwań na drodze, lecz dokładaniem kolejnej "kuli u nogi". Nie przepadam za tego typu zagrywkami, wolę mechanizmy nagradzające i angażujące niż karzące i obciążające.
Po trzecie - czasem osada fajnie "siądzie" i gra się super. Człowiek najchętniej zabudowałby całą mapę i się jeszcze pobawił, bo jest tak niesamowicie fajnie... gdyby nie to, że osadę już "wygrał", więc po co przeciągać, jak nic to już nie daje. Niby można grać dalej, ale nie ma wyzwań, więc nie ma też radochy. Bardzo chciałbym by w grze pojawił się jakiś tryb "długich osad" czyli coś takiego, że jedną osadę można grać i grać i ciągle jest wyzwanie, ciągle ta królowa chce więcej, ciągle są budynki do zdobycia a mieszkańcy robią się bardziej arystokratyczni i byle co im już nie wystarcza. Taki trochę endgame, ale w ramach pojedynczej rozgrywki. To właśnie trochę zapewnia tryb Prestiż 1, ale szkoda, że kolejne już nie. Gdybym miał jedno życzenie - chciałbym, by kolejne DLC (o ile będzie) poszło w tym kierunku.

No i na koniec mankament tej całej losowości - w końcu się ona kończy. Poznasz grę tak dobrze, że przestanie Cię zaskakiwać. A tym samym straci połowę swojego uroku. Czy warto grać dalej, skoro znasz każde zagrożenie, umiesz handlować i znajdować wyjścia z każdych sytuacji? Warto, ale to już nie to samo. Po pewnym czasie zauważysz, że pewne rozwiązania sprawdzają się lepiej niż inne, więc po co kombinować, jak prawie każdą rozgrywkę można wygrać na jeden/dwa sposoby, które opanowałeś do perfekcji. Nie jest to jednak duży minus, bo zanim ta chwila nastąpi mija masa świetnie spędzonych godzin z tytułem.

Zatem - co gra oferuje? 
Świetną baśniową grafikę, klimatyczną muzykę, tonę mechanik do zabawy, urok, chęć spróbowania "kolejnej osady". 
Gra ma głębię i masę zawartości (która niestety w końcu się kończy). Jest niezwykle oryginalna i pomysłowa, lecz dosyć niszowa ze względu na specyficzne połączenie gatunków. Dla mnie to plus, bo uwielbiam, gdy gra nie powstaje "dla każdego". Oznacza to dla mnie, że twórcy zamiast liczyć finanse w excelu zakasali rękawy i zabrali się porządnie za mechaniki - a w obranej przez siebie niszy doszlifowali tytuł. W Against the Storm właśnie tak jest i to czuć.

So, as I said, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game, no matter the price. Up to this point, I haven't played a strategy game mixed with roguelite and devs made a really great choice with that. Roguelite elements fit very well: permament upgrades, picking 3 buildings at the beginning, randomized conditions and cycles. Everything fits very well together and keep every city different.

The art style is solid and fits the vibe. It looks nice in general, but don't expect anything outstanding or groundbreaking. That's not an issue for me though. Game runs smoothly. I didn't experience any bugs or drops in performance.

I felt overwhelmed with all the information that I need to know - different types of resources, production chains, what each building is producing, what you need to produce these things, how to get them and which building can collect it. Additionally, every type of citizen eats different food and has different needs... that's a lot and for me it was too much at once. I didn't find tutorial helpful, it was just brief showcase of 'so you have all this stuff, you need them or you lose, bye!'. After 6 hours systems clicked for me and I started to understand what is what. 

I'm glad that I didn't give up on this game, because it's a great strategy for people who doesn't have a lot of time to play. I will definitely come back to it at some point (once I catch up on my backlog a bit) and play it for time to time, when I have few minutes before the bed - it will be enough for one session, which is more than welcome in the era of big open worlds. However, for the sake of new players, in my opinion tutorial needs to be enhanced, systems needs to be explained in more details and guidance should be more strict in first 2-3 cities/settlements. Talking to your aunt helps a little bit, but it wasn't enough for me. 

Nevertheless, if you're thinking of buying this game, I can definitely recommend it. It's a citybuilder roguelike!

You have 45~120 minutes to accomplish the goals set for you. Doing so requires building a quaint little settlement and actively managing the town until your villagers fail or succeed. The core feature is moral, and losing too much moral means losing the run. All resources are randomized and you will have to competently choose upgrades and additions to your village that take advantage of what resources do appear. Overall this game is quaint, smooth, and satisfying. Watching your village expand into a successful town is a strong formula for a roguelike, and most importantly when your run is complete the settlement provides significant benefits for your meta-progression beyond individual runs.

Villagers are fascinatingly designed with many different benefits per species you are given, or that you choose to begin a run with. Beavers obviously cut wood faster, but Harpies are very easy to please and maintain high moral. The minmaxing required to make your villagers happy and maintain moral is very fun, and encourages diverse settlements that normally might seem unappealing.

Town-building is by far the most gratifying element to me. Each settlement will have a core layout that you operate under, and additions of roads and satellite buildings get you directed towards future developments. Resources naturally cause structures to create districts for your town, with heavy foresting efforts requiring beaver houses and wood storage units. Farming districts require space and specific resource nodes, so having the humans live together in those areas is pleasant to organize.

I never thought it would be possible to make a satisfying version of a citybuilder where you lose all your city's progress repeatedly. Against The Storm pulls it off because the meta-progression from finishing a run is far more impactful and allows you tackle higher difficulties much more reasonably. My sadness at losing the settlement I spent ~120 minutes working on is replaced with joy for the new benefits and power ups I get to make my next settlement easier.

The only gripe I have is that the game can feel a little too punishing at times. Sometimes you can lose a run because of a fundamental error that happened far too early for you to realize its negative effects. Death by a thousand cuts that you feel like are impossible to prevent can be a bit grating and frustrating.

Po dlouhé době skutečně skvělá strategická hra, která je kombinací Settlers, Dungeon Keepera a Warcraft 3 (tam to platí i pro grafiku), lehce i Age of Empires. S nikým ale nebojujete. Bojujete pouze s nastavením své vesnice a tokem surovin a časem, během kterého se zvedá nevraživost lesa (globální debuff), který máte pořád více a více vytěžený. Pár nových věcí navíc jakože vaše hlavní tábořiště (srdce města) spaluje neustále palivo, aby mohlo fungovat (hořet a generovat teplo). Musíte tedy pořád něco dělat, abyste zajistili úplně základní věc neustálý přísun paliva do hlavního ohně a pak řešíte vše ostatní. Skvělý systém "rogue-lite", který všem starým strategiím chyběl je zde naprosto klíčový pro občasné hraní. Hrajete prostě kdy chcete, jednu "session" na 20-40 minut. Pak to dohrajete a klidně odložíte na měsíc, nebo si dáte zase jednu hru další den. Stačí Vám pochopit jen tutorial na začátku (typy budov a principy přidělování dělníků do budov). Jakmile toto pochopíte, můžete se kdykoliv vrátit a prostě si oddechnout u skvělé fantasy budovatelské hry, která Vás za jednu herní jednotku neustále nutí něco zlepšovat a nad něčím přemýšlet. Vybíráte nové "karty (talenty)" schopností a buffů, děláte rozhodnutí, kterou kartu si zvolíte pro další vývoj. Hledáte poklady a oltáře, kterými si otvíráte nové buffy nebo debuffy, plníte úkoly a posunujete se k cíli. Když přijede obchodník do vesnice může vám prodat suroviny, Jantar (pryskiřicové platidlo pro královnu) a nebo si od něj koupit legendární buff nebo výrobnu. Někdy to vyjde a někdy to prohrajete. Ale tím, že je to rogue-lite to můžete zkoušet znovu a být lepší a lepší a prohrávat méně. Myslel jsem si, že v roce 2025 jsou podobné typy her již mrtvé, ale toto je skvělý titul, který dokázal vzít to nejlepší ze všeho a spojit to do příležitostného hraní, které funguje. Během té půl hodiny hraní Vás hra úplně pohltí, protože se snažíte "vyšperkovat - optimalizovat" svůj výrobní a logistický řetězec k úplně dokonalosti a je po celou dobu co zlepšovat. What if you played the early base building phase of an RTS, and then the moment managing it would become tedious or boring, you could move on and do it again? This is the loop of Against the Storm, with the added spice of making limited selections from a randomized deck of villagers and buildings each game. Instead of repeating muscle memory build orders, you must select the best buildings available to suit the needs of your semi-random villagers in the biome you were dealt. You constantly make interesting choices based on your strategy or the bottle necks in your supply chains. It's a chill, comfy time with enough variety and requiring enough brain power in each game (an hour or less) to keep it fresh and engaging every time. An ideal way to wind down after work.

At the time of writing, I am still very early on and playing without expansions, but I can already tell this is likely going to be one I return to again and again.

So far enjoyable, a significant amount of build options might make the start overwhelming. However, as you play you get a feel for how to recover overbuilding or pivoting to other resources. Pretty fun.

It's one of those games where you tell yourself that you'll just play a little longer, and when you glance at a clock, three more hours have gone by. And you keep playing just a little bit more and three hours go by every single time.

AtS is completely absorbing in every respect. The base building is fun, the fantasy waterworld steampunk aesthetic is perfect, the crafting and trading system is intricate, the difficulty is just on the right side of punishing, and the metagame progression and prestige difficulties offer a thousand hours of gameplay if you want them.

The crafting and recipe system, when you first run into it, is completely overwhelming. Each recipe has two or three ingredient slots, and each slot has three to six options, leading to a huge variety of possible ways to make that item. Crafting buildings each come with three recipes for different items, and there are lots of overlaps and weird combinations across all the buildings. You choose blueprints for crafting buildings from small random pools, and the resources you'll find on the map are somewhat random and variable as well, which helps make every run unique. And that's before discussing all of the other modifiers that appear each run: harmful and beneficial forest conditions, perks that tweak your economy, and cornerstone modifiers offered as time goes by. Plus biome specific variants for all of these.

The DLCs are a little thin for the price, each offering one new fantasy species for your villagers, and a couple of new biomes each with mechanical tweaks. These new map terrains give the game a lot of longevity, since each map takes a good few hours to play and there are many biomes in the game now, you'll go many runs without seeing some biomes, which makes it fresh to run into them later. It's good, but at $20, you're only getting the DLC if you're in love with the base game and want to maximize your time with it.

At this writing I'm just over a hundred hours deep in the game, and I've only made it through half of the meta-game tech tree. I'm going into the third of eight "seal" missions, the extra tough scenarios which each cap off a run. And, I've just finished my first map on "prestige 1" difficulty, which now leads me to understand that everything up to and including prestige 1 has just been a tutorial for the remaining prestige difficulties, up to 20. Soon, I look forward to playing the game for real!

But you can have the experience of AtS without reaching for the high difficulties. Start from a tiny settlement, creep into the hostile forest, carve out space for a city, keep all of your little fantasy species villagers happy (or at least keep them from active mutiny), boggle at all of the options for economic development, and manage a horrifying eldritch forest crisis or two before it ends your town. It's really frickin' good.

Try the demo - if you like the vibe and gameplay loop there, you'll enjoy the main game.

I think the trailer is a little misleading (at least for the first 10 to 20 hours). The "enemies" don't really attack you or anything, they're just resource/engine checks that will punish or kill your villagers should you fail. So, if you primarily enjoy town logistics + resource production optimization, you'll probably find it very pleasing.

The game throws a LOT at you right out of the gate, but you don't need to understand most of it to "clear" the early levels. Which means you can kind of take it at your own pace how deeply you want to dive into the game's systems.

I've only just started to get better at the macro management of my recipes + build orders, but it's very cool to see your loops start to really click as you get better at the game.

A tip for newer players - rushing opening small glades can actually be rather punishing in a non-obvious way. They increase hostility by a fair amount, which can then snowball into making your mid game a lot more difficult than it needs to be. The bigger "danger" glades usually give you a lot more resources, and you can time opening them around when a trader shows up to panic buy any key resources you need. Try to focus on being really scrappy with your early game if you notice you're rocketing up hostility way more than you feel capable of dealing with. Good luck!

Эта игра среди всей моей коллекции разных стратегий вызывает самые яркие эмоции и впечатления из-за такой гнетущей, но вдохновляющей атмосферы.
-Много интересных рас, особенно с ДЛС каждый забег становится еще интереснее от самых разных комбинаций и разного стартового лута и способностей каждой расы при прокачке(это же еще и роглайт немножко :)). Каждого корми, развлекай и заставляй работать как и в любых других симуляторах колоний.  -Менеджмент буквально всего : от того чем ты будешь кормить ребят, до мельчайших деталей как использовать разные ресурсы в самых разных зданиях для работы.  Сделано это достаточно удобно, есть разные графики, не разберется только человек далёкий от жанра. Десница королевы одобряет.
-Огромная реиграбельность. Игра не успевает надоесть. Обычный забег идет 30-60 минут +- в зависимости от вашего темпа. Самый долгий забег на самой тяжелой сложности с кучей негативных модификаторов идет может часа 3 в среднем. Существует огромное количество самых разных ивентов, которые будут требовать самых разных решений. Поверьте, вы никогда не пойдете одним и тем же путем дважды. Всегда будут разные условия. Выиграть стратегий много - через задания, открытие полян, торговлю, высокое настроение...Чаще вы будете балансировать между тем, что проще в конкретный момент. От того и получается эта реиграбельность.
Еще один плюс - эта игра работает даже на картошке. Ноутбук совсем не игровой, работает игра может не так плавно как могла бы на топовых ПК, но оптимизация шикарна.

Hands down, this is an incredible game! So much fun! I keep coming back to it, even after having unlocked most everything. The game feels fresh every time thanks to the randomization of objectives and blueprints. If you're looking for a management game with a smattering of rouge-like elements, there's a good chance you'll love this game. Well worth every penny.

Here's how it works:

First, you pick a place to drop a settlement outside the main city hub. Each tile can be a different biome, and the resources available on those tiles will vary based on the biome. You will also get a few different settlers. Their races matter because each race has pros and cons. Each settlement will have a maximum of three different races, and you are only ever guaranteed the races you choose at the start of a settlement. Other races gained will be random.

Then, once you've picked a spot, you load into a Glade. A Glade in this game is an area surrounded by trees. Glades are covered by fog of war, so the only way to see what resources are in one is to cut away the trees obscuring your view. There are small glades which are relatively safe but that contain less resources, and large glades which are relatively dangerous but that may contain more resources. You'll need to consider your settlement's strength and resources before breaking into a larger glade.

Which leads me to the next point: FIRE! Your town is situated around a hearth. The hearth is a requirement for your town's people, and it therefore will need a hearthkeeper and fuel. There are a few different fuels available, but by far the most abundant and easy to access fuel is timber, a resource provided by your logging camps. Your hearth will provide some relative safety for your town at the cost of fuel. Running out of fuel is a sure-fire way to have a bad time.

The forest, however, is always watching you. There is a meter at the top of your screen which measures the forest's hostility. It climbs for a number of different reasons, one of which being logging. Another being opening glades. Hostility lowers your town's people's happiness. If your town's people's happiness goes into the negative for any one race, then members of that race will emigrate away from your settlement. Emigration (and colonist death) grates on the queen's nerves, so you'll notice that the queen's patience will grow more and more strained the more you hemorrhage town's people.

The Queen's patience is what you have to manage if you want to keep your town operating for long enough to fill your reputation bar (once filled, you have 'won' the round). If the queen loses all of her patience, then you 'lose' that round. You'll often find that the queen is a difficult person to please, and that she has very little leeway to offer her viceroy's (you).

You're town will need buildings, agriculture, and industry if you're going to support your town's folk. The buildings that will be available to you are determined from a set of cards dealt to you. This keeps the game fresh as it forces you to develop on-the-fly strategies rather than just sticking to one tried and true method. As far as I've noticed, there is no one building that is over powered, nor is there any one building that will tank your run. Its all very balanced, but that still won't guarantee you a win. Sometimes the forest will simply outclass you.

Once you've won (or lost) a round, you will need to pick a different tile to settle. This is the core game loop. You're settlements will eventually get wiped off the map when the big storm comes at the end of the cycle (you can see the cycle's timeline at the bottom of your screen on the world map). The end of the cycle means that all your city tiles will be destroyed, and that you will have to start over. Reforging a seal in a sealed forest will extend the time in a cycle, but don't worry about that at first.

Your goal in the early game is to collect as much bread and other resources to trade at the city hub. The city hub will offer you a number of different bonuses, boons, and advantages, so make good use of them! 

Your goal in the mid to late game is to make it to the sealed forest (boss level), and to reforge the seal. Sealed forest levels are very difficult, so don't get discouraged if you fail. Use your earned revenue to buy upgrades in the capital and learn from your mistakes so you don't fail the same way again.

Against the Storm fue una sorpresa para mí. Empecé pensando que era un juego de construcción de bases y recolección de recursos hasta que me vi envuelta en una gestión de supervivencia con recursos y eventos generados de forma aleatoria con una dificultad que va escalando progresivamente. Tiene una dirección de arte steampunk muy bonita y un diseño de personajes muy originales. 

Como pionero de la Ciudadela Ardiente en un mundo azotado por una tormenta sin fin debes usar todos los recursos a tu disposición para sobrevivir y salvar el reino. La Reina te envía a las tierras que se extienden fuera de la cálida y segura capital como expedicionario avanzado para que vayas creando asentamientos cada vez más alejados. Puedes elegir la dirección que quieras en tu primera incursión, se te permite ver los recursos, modificaciones del terreno y otras características de la zona donde quieres jugar. Cuanto más te alejes de la Ciudadela, más complicado se volverá todo: menos recursos, modificadores más exigentes, más peligros, más cosas en contra... pero mejores premios, evidentemente. Tu objetivo es encontrar unos sellos ancestrales y completar el asentamiento donde están, cumpliendo la misión principal. Todavía no sé lo que pasa cuando los consigues todos, solo he completado tres sellos.

El sistema se repite en ciclos. Sales de la Capital para crear tu asentamiento, eliges donde empezar y cuando entras, los recursos y eventos del mapa se generan de manera aleatoria. El objetivo de cada asentamiento es alcanzar un nivel de Determinación antes de que la Impaciencia de la Reina, que va subiendo con el tiempo, llegue al mismo número. Eso pondrá fin a la Incursión actual. Para llegar al objetivo tienes un número fijo de Pobladores (un máximo de tres razas, puedes tener el número total que quieras) en un claro rodeado de niebla de guerra; solo puedes despejar la niebla talando árboles para abrir nuevos claros. Estos claros pueden tener recursos (pequeños o grandes) o eventos (buenos o malos), y siempre es aleatorio. Si talas árboles, sube la Hostilidad del bosque; a más Hostilidad, la Impaciencia sube y la Determinación baja. Tus pobladores deben estar felices, cuidados y alimentados, o su Determinación bajará, comenzarán a marcharse, a fallecer; eso retrasará tu producción de comida o recursos, lo que provocará que baje la Determinación y suba la Impaciencia, que a su vez  causará que te quedes sin recursos para que los pocos pobladores que te quedan puedan sobrevivir. ¿He hablado ya de la lluvia? Cuando llueve, baja la Determinación. Cuando sale el sol, simplemente no baja pero tampoco sube. Un evento en un claro puede causar que tus pobladores se mueran de un susto, otro puede hacer que la Impaciencia suba el doble de lo normal; puedes quedar maldito el resto de la incursión si no resuelves los eventos a tiempo. ¿Me sigues? Cada mapa es una lucha de gestión constante contra absolutamente todas las mecánicas que tiene el juego. Esto se repetirá con cada asentamiento y como estarás cada vez un poco más lejos que antes, la dificultad crece, porque viene determinada por la distancia de la Ciudadela. Los biomas serán una pesadilla más que gestionar junto con el ánimo de los Pobladores, los recursos o las maldiciones ancestrales que descubras sin querer por salir a buscar más recursos. Y no voy a hablar de lo que pasa con la podedrumbre. Es mejor que lo descubras por tu cuenta :) 

Los asentamientos se pueden ganar de varias formas. Aunque el objetivo es ganar Determinación, tienes varias opciones; si no puedes hacerlo de una manera, podrás cambiar a otra, aunque requiere cierta práctica y mucho ensayo y error. Deberás elegir con cuidado cada movimiento, es muy fácil que un asentamiento controlado acabe en desastre si cometes un error de cálculo o no tienes en cuenta los peligros de los claros. Cuentas con mucha información que te permite gestionar la generación y el consumo de recursos, así como la opción de deshabilitar producciones si lo necesitas. Existen cinco razas de Pobladores (castores, humanos, lagartos...), cada una con una necesidad diferente por cubrir —algunas coinciden entre varias— y habilidades pasivas únicas. Puedes elegir uno o dos tipos de Pobladores de inicio, otros te serán entregados de manera aleatoria y siempre estará limitado a tres razas. 

Cuando alcances la distancia máxima, terminará el ciclo actual de lluvia, donde volverás a la Ciudadela. Recogeras los premios al final del ciclo y podrás desbloquear nuevas mejoras que te harán la vida más fácil: nuevos edificios, bonificadores, recetas y mejoras a lo que ya posees. Tienes una casita que podrás decorar y mejorar, y en esas pausas entre ciclos te contarán la historia de por qué no deja de llover. 

Es un juego dificil pero no te castiga ni te dificulta las cosas de forma artificial. Es decir, sí te castiga en el asentamiento si te descuidas un poco, pero está bien equilibrado. Los mapas de inicio son muy sencillos, los intermedios te enseñarán nuevas mecánicas más complejas sin ser agobiantes pero los asentamientos extremadamente difíciles pueden ser largos y complicados, muy fáciles de perder si no sabes recuperarte. A veces es mejor perder el asentamiento, existe la opción de darlo por perdido si no puedes ganarlo; simplemente no ganarás loot pero podrás avanzar antes de que acabe el ciclo. Puedes quedarte en la periferia del último asentamiento fácil para farmear premios o puedes avanzar hasta lugares super peligrosos para ver qué hay. Tú eliges.  

Me gustaría destacar la música. A mí me resulta relajante para construir cuando todo está tranquilo pero es genial que cambie según el ciclo meteorológico y el bioma o evento con el que te cruzas. Ayuda mucho a concentrarte en el objetivo. Los gráficos son muy sencillitos; tus pobladores son bastante pequeños pero tienen animaciones para casi cada cosa que hacen, y los edificios se diferencian claramente unos de otros por el estilo de arquitectura.

Actualmente hay dos DLC con una raza nueva cada uno (sapos y murciélagos), nuevos mapas, biomas, decoraciones, eventos y minijuegos. El juego base ya cuenta con todo lo que necesitas, son muchas horas de juego para completarlos; si te gusta tener más variedad, los DLC son excelentes adiciones para tus partidas. 

Y eso es todo, ¿alguna pregunta? ¿No? A trabajar antes de que vuelva a llover.

Існує кілька геймплейних схем створення містобудівних симуляторів. Більшість із них можна описати так: гравець будує дедалі ефективніші чи прибутковіші споруди (наприклад, банк чи консервний завод), але він обмежений необхідністю задовольняти потреби жителів (наприклад, їх потрібно кормити, тож потрібен ланцюжок виробничих будівель для створення їжі).

Однак коли в описі містобудівної стратегії згадують механіку rogue-lite, важко уявити, як розробники могли б реалізувати це цікаво. На якому етапі вводитимуться дійсно вагомі варіанти вибору, що не сприйматимуться як несправедливі обмеження? Як гра зможе зробити кожну партію унікальною? Та й чи можна повноцінно насолодитися сесією, яка триває 1.5–2 години, якщо, наприклад, одна партія в ANNO може тривати понад 50 годин?

Виявилося, що в Against the Storm розробники винайшли унікальну формулу, якої раніше ніде не було:
- Мультиресурсність: Досягнення цілей (від зведення нової будівлі до задоволення потреб жителів) потребує унікальної комбінації ресурсів. Наприклад, м'ясо + борошно або дошки + тканина.
- Варіативність ресурсних будівель: У грі існує велика кількість будівель, кожна з яких дозволяє добувати ресурси у певній комбінації та з різною ефективністю. Наприклад, в одній будівлі можна виготовляти дошки з ефективністю 2 і борошно з ефективністю 1, а в іншій - лише дошки, але з ефективністю 3, та додатково цеглу з ефективністю 2.
- Обмеження ресрусів на мапі: Кожна мапа створює нові комбінації ресурсів, що змушує адаптуватися і постійно відчувати дефіцит.
- Стратегічний вибір креслень: До будівель ми отримуємо доступ поступово, залежно від наших успіхів. При цьому, коли з’являється можливість обрати нове креслення, ми можемо взяти лише одне. Це і є ключовий елемент rogue-lite вибору: ми змушені обирати будівлі, що дають доступ до дефіцитних ресурсів. Буває, що будівля не потрібна зараз, але ми беремо її «на виріст». А буває, що хорошого варіанту немає взагалі, тож доводиться обирати з того, що є, і повністю змінювати стратегію партії.

У поєднанні з великою кількістю інших механік, спрямованих на те, щоб гравець постійно ризикував або підлаштовувався під ситуацію, кожна партія дійсно стає унікальною та захопливою.

Я отримав від гри багато задоволення, але радше як від менеджмент-головоломки, ніж від містобудівної стратегії. На жаль, багато будівель візуально схожі між собою, їхні спеціалізації погано зчитуються візуально, а можливість створювати естетично привабливі містечка втрачається в постійних перегонах за ресурсами. Проте цей унікальний менеджмент ресурсів через розбудову міста, велике різноманіття ігрових ситуацій і можливостей та чудово пропрацьований інтерфейс створюють справді чудовий ігровий процес.

**A Roguelite City Builder That Actually Feels Alive**

I’ve put about 27 hours into *Against the Storm*, and it still feels like I’ve barely scratched the surface—which, for this kind of game, is exactly what you want.

What immediately stands out is how fresh every run feels. The RNG systems aren’t just there for variety—they actively reshape your strategy. You’re not executing a fixed plan; you’re constantly negotiating with the world, adapting to what it gives (and withholds). That creates a kind of tension and dynamism that most city builders never reach.

The focus on small, temporary settlements instead of sprawling mega-cities is a brilliant twist. Each town feels like a self-contained puzzle with its own identity, constraints, and story. There’s something satisfying about building under pressure, knowing you won’t be there forever. It turns optimization into something more… urgent, almost survival-like.

Atmosphere is another huge win. The world has this mystical, slightly oppressive tone—like nature is watching you, not just surrounding you. It gives weight to your decisions and makes the environment feel like an active participant rather than just a backdrop.

That said, there are a few areas where the game could grow:

* The UI could be more readable and streamlined, especially as complexity ramps up.
* Tutorials could do a better job preparing players for higher difficulty play.
* And while the world is rich in mood, I’d love to see a stronger central narrative or story thread tying everything together.

Overall, this is one of the most unique and engaging strategy experiences I’ve played in a long time. It doesn’t just iterate on the genre—it bends it into something new.

Highly recommended, especially if you enjoy strategy games that force you to think on your feet rather than follow a script.

    Очень понравился стиль тёмного фэнтези, небольшая доля стимпанка, достаточно гнетущая атмосфера, реализация и глубина игры. Сюжет здесь маленький, но лично для меня в основе своей важен геймплей. В мире есть природный катаклизм, который в буквальном смысле "стирает" поселения с лица земли каждый цикл. В "живых" остаётся лишь центральный город во главе с Королевой. Вы - наместник, которому поручено выдвинуться в экспедицию, основать и развить поселение, которое принесёт ресурсы великому ранее описанному городу.
    В игре присутствует обучение, достаточно быстро можно освоить все механики игры. Интерфейс не перегружен, все опции на удобных местах, присутствуют удобные горячие клавиши для многих функций.
    В отдельности хочется отметить хорошие решения по введению сложностей игры. Базовых сложностей здесь четыре, но когда поиграл в игру приличное количество времени они будут казаться совсем детскими. Здесь же присутствует следующий этап сложностей (Престиж), добавляя целых 20 уровней сложности (каждый уровень - плюс одно усложнение в определённом аспекте игры), что даёт вызов в каждой сессии любителям хардкора.
    Сам геймплей выглядит так: есть глобальная клетчатая карта, в её центре всегда основной город, от которого вы выбираете, где начать основывать своё поселение. Эти клетки разные (в игре присутствует некоторое количество видов биомов, в которых кардинально от друг друга отличаются природные условия и находящиеся там ресурсы). Также, на карте присутствуют клетки усложнений и бонусов, если стартовать вплотную с такой клеткой, на всю игровую сессию вы получаете собственно дополнительный аспект. Есть клетки "заданий", где мы встречаем какое-нибудь явление или существо, которое даёт нам задание на сессию, а за его успешное выполнение вам даются приятные бонусы или ресурсы как правило на следующие сессии в рамках цикла. После выбора клетки снабжаем на выбор наш караван и в путь!
    Пока вы не в режиме сессии, вы можете заходить в основной город. Там есть несколько разделов, например таких как Достижения и Улучшения. Т.е. у нас есть множество целей (за их выполнение открываются некоторые элементы геймплея) и возможность прокачать некоторые моменты, облегчая себе жизнь на все будущие сессии (что-то вроде ускорения ходьбы жителей на 1%, прибытие торговца на 2% быстрее и т.д.). Прокачка идёт за отдельные 3 вида ресурсов, которые даются по результатам в конце каждой сессии (чем выше у вас выбрана сложность, тем больше этих ресурсов даётся). 
    Из основных механик у нас снизу экрана две основных шкалы - синяя и красная. Синяя - репутация с Королевой, красная же - её нетерпение. Нетерпение растёт всегда, это буквально игра на время. Заполнилась полностью шкала - вы проиграли, Королева вами недовольна, вы подвели Тлеющий город, поселение не выжило - позор, пытайтесь снова. Нетерпение растёт всегда, но так же может увеличиваться от ваших косяков, принятых решений или событий. Репутация повышается за комфортные условия жителей, выполнение различных указов, успешное завершение полянного события. Полная шкала репутации - победа, поселение прошло проверку на выживание, переходим к следующему.
    Стартуем посередине карты с нашими жителями с каравана, ресурсами и с основным зданием и центральным складом. Карта представляет собой множество секторов (полян). Все эти поляны огорожены деревьями и мы не видим их содержимого. Т.е. вскрытие каждой поляны для нас сюрприз, который вынудит принимать те или иные решения.
    Тут нет понятие сражений и открытых столкновений, враждуем мы со временем, гнилью, погодными условиями и различными событиями на вскрытых полянах (их нужно вовремя завершить, иначе быть беде).
    Пытаемся сделать комфортные условия для наших жителей, обеспечить их нужной работой, чтобы они не захотели уйти от ужасного настроя или не умерли от голода или от незавершённого вовремя полянного события.
    Игру можно ставить на паузу для спокойного и детального изучения явлений и происходящего на карте, можно изменять скорость игры: x1, x1,5, x2, x3.
    В общем, случайностей и рандома в игре достаточно, чтобы считать эту игру реиграбельной, есть авантюризм и удовольствие в прохождении, нет ощущения, что каждую игру можно делать одно и то же и это сработает, из-за чего приходится принимать другие решения и идти новым путём процветания с совершенно разными бонусами или усложнениями.
    Спасибо разработчикам за их труд, рекомендую поиграть любителям стратегий, играется сбалансированно интересно и заставляет подумать, учитывать множество факторов для успешного развития.

I like the game, but I think I have had just about enough(for now). Considering I don't really like this kind of strategy games (where you play "matches" or "games" and then start over, I am much more of a permanent base builder kind of person), it's amazing it held me for so long. But now the randomness is really getting to me. I either get a super easy game when everything aligns, or super bad game where RNG just keeps screwing me. Then I cannot complete orders, cannot make anything relevant for my population to raise resolve, so I am stuck for an hour with the 3 starter buildings and no currency(amber, tools) to dig myself out of a hole, and it's just super frustrating not being able to do anything.

I have jumped to higher difficulties quite early, played always at least on Pioneer, and shortly after reforging the Bronze seal I switched to Veteran. But now, after closing the Silver seal, it looks like I am expected to go up to Viceroy, and things are falling apart. 
At level 12 I am still lacking a ton of things from the upgrades tree, things that would balance out a lot of the increasing randomness I presume(field kitchen for some inefficient complex food making, race abilities, extra rerolls, more choices, timed orders, etc.). But even playing on what I considered higher difficulties, jumping to complete any event(modifier) on the world map I could reach, I still don't get nearly enough currency to make the upgrades keep up with my level. My average upgrade level is around 9, or 9.5. 
I really wish the currency drop would keep up the experience gain, because I don't really understand what more I could do. I crammed in as many games per each cycle(90% of games I finished between years 6 to 8), on as high difficulty I could manage, with as many modifiers I could find on the map, and it still isn't nearly enough.

The mechanics of the game are super deep, but a lot of it depends on you being able to get off the ground at the beginning. A lot of the times I realize too late, there were better possibilities than what I have done, that could have made me win sooner, or that could have made the game a lot easier. But there is so much stuff to keep an eye on, it was impossible to stay on top of it all.
The ability to use many things in a single recipe is genius, but it also makes a lot of things unpredictable, and impossible to keep on top of. A resource that I had a lot of is suddenly completely gone, because I enabled its usage in too many buildings, and it snowballs into a huge issue.
Each biome has different set of available resources, and it drastically changes things.
Each race changes things a lot, and synergizing their needs seems essential. Stuff like having lizards + foxes, and being able to make skewers or pickled goods early. Harpies are the worst crybabies, and I hate getting them as one of the three races. They make everything harder instantly. They are the first ones to leave the settlement.
The hostility multiplier on Viceroy and higher difficulties are completely crazy.

My big pet peeve with this game is trading. Traders often offer a lot of resources you can't get to at the moment, but the exchange rates are so bad, they are unusable. It makes me not want to interact with them most of the time. At the beginning you barely have anything to trade with, and once your settlement is good enough to start selling things for amber, you usually don't need the resource part of trading anymore and just hunt for extra cornerstones or blueprints.

Overall, I think the game is good, but I am not exactly the target audience. I don't imagine myself ever going into the prestige difficulties, and I have no idea how people handle prestige 20.

222小时打通艾德曼合金封印，真的是一款不错的游戏。这个游戏抉择很多，从威望11以上开始基本就必须根据蓝图和地图资源规划好发展路线了，威望16以上容错开始变小且负反馈开始变大，但多熟悉几局还是能稳住节奏发展起来。说一下新手容易犯难的点，这个游戏不管是前期引导还是指令设计都没有突出贸易和服务的作用（尤其是指令，只看短期收益的话基本纯副作用），这就导致威望10以前玩家可能都只想着靠工具开贮藏库过关。10声望过关的情况下这确实是最简单方便的通关方式，一旦威望上去，需要18声望的时候，这种策略就是纯粹的画地为牢。调整思路、探索不同的发展方式才是这个游戏最正确的玩法。我个人的经验是：威望之前的难度找工具探图打熟悉各种事件的解决方式（以及超时后果）威望10以下，尝试商人和贸易路线（个人感觉是最爽且正反馈最大的时期），威望11以上控敌意，多用偏袒偷声望，蓝图和指令选择尽量舍弃保守选项，一切抉择为了能最终成型发展路线服务（初始工作站能制造的材料就不要再为了省拿点原材料选蓝图了，车间是最大的陷阱）。完成定居点的发展路线有很多，有时候前期一个超模的基石或者限时指令基本就能确定整把的胜利方程式，熟悉之后就会发现这个游戏能赢的方式数不胜数。除了指令和基石，还有些建筑也能直接帮你高效完成定居点，点名表扬神殿（配合造油的建筑持续烧油，只要循环起来整把都不用担心敌意影响），说实话服务建筑都挺超模的，但神殿在这里面应该是最超模的一个了，越是高难越能彰显神殿的含金量。最后再说说这个游戏的种族设计和DLC，根据种族设定特色建筑这方面简直是天才设计，合适的地形选择合适的种族就能事半功倍，或者留意初始商队种族共通的食物和服务需求，建野外厨房快速获得满意声望后期减少服务建筑的抉择。两个DLC，青蛙和蝙蝠，前者让新来人口更快，能直接加速游戏进程，纯超模；后者强度一半在庄园法庭上（最简单有效的控敌意手段，生产加倍和这比起来都算是添头了），另一半在血价合约和同类相食上。但说白了这俩都属于锦上添花的东西，也就图一乐，真正的T0幻神还得是狐狸，狐神有着高贵的群体满意和护火降低空地敌意以及最关键的加速事件解决，我最后打艾德曼合金封印的时候，狐神配合远见和两级海洋燃料献祭，两分钟一个受禁事件，晴朗季开的俩受禁空地风暴季刚来就打完了，给我都玩笑了。

[h1]Addictive at Its Best, Slightly Too Min-Max Later On[/h1]

Against the Storm is an incredibly addictive resource-management survival roguelike built around short, time-limited runs. In each run, you have a fixed number of days to establish a successful settlement, which creates a constant sense of urgency. You’re not just surviving the storm—you’re racing against time to optimize every decision.

The game is very approachable at the start. Like most management games, you can begin at Settler difficulty and gradually climb higher as you get comfortable. For players looking for a real challenge, the highest difficulty levels provide exactly that, forcing you to think carefully and execute efficiently.

What really stands out is the roguelite design. Each settlement comes with different conditions and challenges, keeping every run feeling fresh. The developers clearly put a lot of thought into making the gameplay loop varied and engaging.

For me, the game felt almost perfect during the first 40 hours. It was hard to put down. However, once I reached Viceroy difficulty, the experience started to lean heavily into min-maxing, which took away some of the enjoyment.

Overall, this is still a very strong and worthwhile game. If you enjoy management games with a sense of pressure and replayability, Against the Storm is easy to recommend—and for many players, it can be seriously addictive.

One thing that struck me as I've been playing is that even after 150+ hours, I've never gotten frustrated. If you're into strategy and getting to control how you play, I highly recommend this.

Closed the Gold Seal last night. If I continue playing - which I probably won't - it would be on the prestige difficulties while chasing the prestige milestones. The game is a roguelite city-builder with some world context, but not a lot of deep story or lore. The idea is to build small towns under harsher and harsher conditions while each successful town gives you resources to upgrade future towns. Overall, it's pretty fun and I enjoyed it. The early games are casual and relaxing while the last ones leading up to the Gold Seal were more challenging. The goal of each town is to reach a certain reputation level before the queen gets too impatient and shuts down your town while also balancing against the general hostility of the forest in which you're settling. There's a lot of randomness to each town, so it has pretty high replayability and no two towns really felt alike to me even when I worked out a general strategy for how to approach building and objective completion. I think I'd give it an 8 or 8.5/10. The game knows what it is and does those things very well.

25 hours in.  Stumbled through several missions until I finally figured out the main premises.  

PROS: 
Love the different challenges and keeping the queen (or whatever she's called) happy.  
I enjoy how every level is has different resources.  
It's also great that the resource buildings can be picked up and moved to newly discovered resources.  

CONS:  
Need Beavers, but never get a reward option to get Beavers?  Guess what, you're ****ed. 

Too specialized for such short missions.  Example: Have an option to get Human-specific housing, but you only have 4 Humans?  Why not go ahead and get that to get 3.2 happiness points?

The missions are so short and there are SO many resources, some of which you can't attain in the time frame (e.g., large pond, but you only have small pond capabilities.)  

The resources are also used to craft multiple different items, with several buildings having overlap in what they can create.  There is so much overlap between which buildings create what and how efficient they are, it becomes tedious to decide which building to get next.  Checking back to see what you already have, what they can build, what you need, etc.
[Should have a sweet hover-over UI that'd show you what buildings are best for your objectives, what you're lacking etc. OR a tab on the main menu showing a flowchart of what's needed for each manufactured item.]

BIGGEST ISSUE: I can NEVER remember exactly what resources I need to build quest items.  DEVs, for God's sake, can you please build a cheat sheet in the game or show the prerequisites for certain items?  
I accept a quest to create a certain number of an item and then find out my level loadout has NONE of the pre-reqs to finish that quest.  
If I was the mayor/manager of that city (which I am supposed to be in the RP) I would clearly know what resources I need to make mead, pies, shoes, or whatever.  However, as the game is, I have to just pick an option and hope and pray I find the right resources.

OVERALL: 
I give the game a thumbs-up.  But the pluses are also the minuses.  
Fun new challenge every time?  COOL!
Tedious endless struggle to figure out how the hell to get what you need to please the queen?  POO.
