[h1] V RISING É UM DOS MELHORES JOGOS DE VAMPIRO QUE EU JÁ JOGUEI [/h1]

Se tem uma coisa que V Rising faz muito bem, é te convencer de que você realmente é um vampiro.

Não apenas alguém com poderes.

Um vampiro.

Você acorda enfraquecido, precisa reconstruir seu castelo, caçar sangue para sobreviver e evitar a luz do sol a qualquer custo.

É uma fantasia que poucos jogos conseguiram entregar tão bem.

A primeira coisa que me conquistou foi o combate.

Ele é extremamente fluido.

Cada habilidade tem impacto, esquivar na hora certa faz toda a diferença e enfrentar chefes exige atenção de verdade.

Não basta chegar apertando qualquer botão.

Você precisa aprender os padrões dos inimigos, administrar suas habilidades e aproveitar cada oportunidade.

Cada vitória parece merecida.

Outro aspecto fantástico é a progressão.

Em vez de simplesmente subir de nível, você derrota chefes espalhados pelo mapa para aprender novas habilidades, desbloquear estruturas e expandir seu castelo.

Essa sensação de evolução é extremamente recompensadora.

Sempre existe um novo objetivo chamando sua atenção.

O sistema de construção também me surpreendeu.

Montar o próprio castelo é viciante.

Você organiza salas, cria oficinas, melhora equipamentos, instala laboratórios e transforma uma simples ruína em uma fortaleza gigantesca.

Passei muito mais tempo decorando e reorganizando meu castelo do que imaginava.

A exploração também merece muitos elogios.

O mapa é enorme, cheio de biomas diferentes, fortalezas, vilarejos, cavernas e segredos.

Cada nova região apresenta desafios próprios e incentiva você a ficar cada vez mais forte antes de seguir adiante.

Outro detalhe que adorei foi a mecânica do sangue.

Cada tipo oferece bônus diferentes, fazendo com que escolher a próxima vítima também faça parte da estratégia.

É uma ideia simples, mas que adiciona muita personalidade ao jogo.

Visualmente, V Rising é muito bonito.

As florestas sombrias, os cemitérios, as fortalezas e os castelos criam uma atmosfera perfeita para esse universo.

Tudo combina muito bem com a proposta gótica da aventura.

A trilha sonora acompanha esse clima com excelência.

Ela reforça a sensação de mistério durante a exploração e cresce nos confrontos mais importantes.

Agora...

Se existe um ponto que pode incomodar algumas pessoas, é o ritmo inicial.

As primeiras horas exigem bastante coleta de recursos e construção antes que todas as mecânicas estejam disponíveis.

Também existe um pouco de repetição na busca por materiais durante determinados momentos da campanha.

Mas, sinceramente...

Nunca achei isso suficiente para diminuir minha diversão.

Porque o restante do jogo compensa com sobra.

No fim das contas, V Rising entrega uma das melhores fantasias de vampiro que já encontrei em um videogame.

O combate é excelente.

A progressão é extremamente viciante.

Os chefes são memoráveis.

Construir seu castelo é divertido.

E explorar aquele mundo sombrio sempre recompensa a curiosidade.

Depois de terminar, ficou claro para mim que V Rising não é apenas um ótimo jogo de sobrevivência.

É um dos melhores jogos de vampiro já feitos.

E uma recomendação muito fácil para qualquer pessoa que goste desse universo.

I originally picked up V Rising because the idea of combining survival mechanics with Hack and Slash combat sounded interesting, and it turned out to be one of the biggest positive surprises I've had in the genre. I played most of it solo, but I also spent a good amount of time in co-op with a friend. Both ways of playing are enjoyable, although the experience feels slightly different depending on whether you're building your vampire empire alone or with someone else.

The combat is easily one of the game's strongest aspects. It has a fast pace, responsive controls, and a wide variety of weapons, spells, and abilities that encourage experimenting with different playstyles. Boss fights are particularly enjoyable. Every V Blood boss introduces unique mechanics and rewards you with new powers, recipes, or crafting stations, making progression feel meaningful instead of simply increasing your numbers.

The survival mechanics never felt overwhelming to me. You still need to gather resources, refine materials, and manage your equipment, but the game keeps introducing new tools and upgrades that make the grind feel rewarding. Rather than surviving just for the sake of surviving, you're constantly working toward expanding your vampire castle and unlocking new technologies.

Castle building deserves special praise. It's surprisingly deep and gives you a lot of freedom to create a home that not only looks good but also serves practical purposes. Organizing crafting stations, decorating rooms, and gradually transforming a small fortress into a massive vampire castle became one of my favorite parts of the game.

Exploration is also handled very well. Every new region introduces stronger enemies, different resources, and increasingly difficult bosses. Because progression is tied to defeating specific enemies, exploring the world always has a purpose. I rarely felt like I was wandering around without a goal.

Another thing I really appreciated was the value for money. I bought the game for very little compared to how many hours I ended up playing. It's one of those rare games where I constantly felt I was getting far more content than I paid for.

If I had one criticism, it's that the later stages can become somewhat grindy, especially when farming resources for higher-tier equipment. Depending on your server settings or whether you're playing solo, some crafting timers and material requirements may also start to feel a bit repetitive. Fortunately, the gameplay loop remained enjoyable enough that it never became a dealbreaker for me.

Pros:

+ Excellent blend of survival and action RPG mechanics
+ Fast, responsive, and satisfying combat
+ Great variety of weapons, spells, and builds
+ Rewarding V Blood boss progression
+ Deep and addictive castle-building system

Cons:

- Endgame can become grindy
- Resource farming occasionally slows the pacing
- Some crafting timers can feel unnecessary when playing solo

V Rising perfectly captures the atmosphere of a dark, gothic, vampire-infested world. From gorgeous art direction to distinct zone color palettes, the visual design is stunning. It is essentially a compact, Diablo-style action RPG mixed with phenomenal base building.

Dynamic Progression: 
No traditional levels or XP. Progression is tied directly to boss kills, forcing you to master mechanics rather than over-level by grinding.

Awesome Castle Customization:
Base building is surprisingly addictive. The gorgeous artwork naturally motivates you to pause your journey, remodel, and spend hours designing a fancy vampire estate.

Flexible Difficulty Sliders: While the raw item grind can be tedious, developer-provided resource drop sliders let you skip the farming and save time so you can enjoy the other activities.

Challenging Boss Design: 
Boss encounters are tough, creative, and mechanically deep. Some acts act as real skill checks, requiring tactical re-specing and community build guides to crack.

Slow Traversal: 
Early-game foot travel feels sluggish. Horses feel unlocked a bit too late, and the game-changing Bat Form arrives at the absolute endgame.

Linear Structure:
Because everything unlocks via specific bosses, the game progression can feel a bit linear and limited. You dont have much choice here. You follow the predefined path.

Vague Story:
The lore is barely there. A few Elden Ring-style NPCs with cryptic dialogue would have made the world feel much more impactful.

[b] Summary: 8/10 [b/]
If you are on the fence, wishlist it and wait for a sale. Snagging this for $15–$20 is an absolute bargain for a long weekend of gaming. Highly recommended!

V Rising vereint mehrere Blickwinkel zu einem stimmigen Gesamterlebnis: düstere Atmosphäre, packende Kämpfe, tiefes Crafting und die Freiheit, ein eigenes Reich zu erschaffen. Die Welt fühlt sich rau, gefährlich und lebendig an, genau das, was man sich von einem Vampir‑Survival‑Game wünscht.

Dadurch entsteht ein wunderbarer Gameplay‑Kreislauf aus Erforschen, Kämpfen, Sammeln und Gestalten.

Im Großen und Ganzen kann ich V Rising jedem empfehlen, der schon immer einmal in die Haut eines Vampirs schlüpfen wollte, mit allem, was dazugehört: Macht, Stil, Dunkelheit und dem Aufbau eines eigenen Reiches. :)

En este juego puedes hacer tu propia base (castillo), tener caballos para viajar rápido, transformarte en animales con habilidades (salvo el sapo, inutil sapo), hacerte armadura, subir de nivel, desbloquear pasivas, hacerte armas, pegarte una y otra vez con los bosses, farmear, hacerte hasta 4 bases mas porque, por qué no, tener sirvientes para mandarlos a por materiales...
Una mecánica interesante del juego, de entre muchas, es que los NPCs tienen un tipo de sangre determinado con una calidad de sangre determinada (RNG), si bebes de ellos, el tipo de sangre te da unas pasivas y segun la calidad mejoran ¿qué es lo chulo? puedes tener prisioneros en tu castillo como esclavos (bueno, como comida) asi que si ves uno que te gusta con calidad de sangre 90 o superior ¡pum! pokebola y a sufrir en mi celda.
Hay distintas dificultades que realmente se sienten, si juegas en brutal como hice yo, los bosses no solo aguantan y pegan mas sino que tienen mas mecánicas. Muy disfrutón.

✔️ [b]Puntos fuertes:[/b]
[b]― Coop[/b] - Puedes jugar con amigos de forma online, de hecho hay servidores muy vivos.
[b]― Cantidad de niveles[/b] – Tienes una progresión larga y además una cantidad de bosses muy considerable, no te vas a cansar.
[b]― Combate[/b] – Según el arma, pegas, además las armas tienen habilidades que puedes usar y luego tienes magias que vas desbloqueando.
[b]― Customización [/b] – Tienes customización de personaje pero es que la customización de la base es espectacular.
[b]― Dificultades[/b] – Desde paseo en el parque a mini souls, tu decides y lo cambias cuando quieras in-game.
[b]― End-game[/b] – Hay boss final pero tu puedes jugar eternamente.
[b]― Idioma [/b] - ¡Está en español!
[b]― Logros[/b] – Hay un poco de todo, nada muy extraño, pero sí que te obliga a pasarte el juego en la mayor dificultad. Yo jugué brutal con 2 amigos y fueron 63h el 100%.

❌ Puntos débiles:
[b]― Ninguno destacable[/b]

If you love base building and the fantasy of being a full‑power, night‑dwelling vampire, V Rising absolutely delivers. The progression system is one of the best parts of the game — no boring XP grind, no endless leveling treadmill. You get stronger by earning better gear, hunting bosses, drinking their V‑blood, and unlocking new powers and crafting stations. It feels clean, rewarding, and genuinely addictive.

The castle building is top‑tier. Your base doesn’t just look cool — it feels like a real extension of your vampiric identity. Every upgrade, every new room, every servant you command adds to that sense of rising power.

Combat is fast, stylish, and surprisingly deep. The world is atmospheric and fun to explore. And the loop of hunt → craft → upgrade → dominate stays satisfying for a long time.

My only real wish is more content. The foundation is so strong that the game practically begs for more regions, bosses, spells, and castle pieces. It’s already great — it could be legendary with more updates.

Das Spiel an sich ist ganz witzig. Es gibt aber zu viele Dinge die mich nerven und auf Dauer zu sehr frustrieren. Die dadurch entstehenden Kopfschmerzen sind für mich persönlich ein Ausschlusskriterium.

Die Welt ist schön und viele Spielmechaniken sind eigentlich gut gemeint und auch spannend.

Leider gibt es beim bauen und crafting den Umstand, dass ich meine Produktion nicht direkt aus den Werkbanken und Co. verbrauchen kann. Ich muss sie entweder mit mir rumtragen oder erst herausnehmen, 5m laufen und im Nachbarraum deponieren, weil Kisten nur in einem speziellen Raum ihren Inhalt teilen können. LOL.
Das führ dauerhaft dazu, dass man wie ein Gummiball durch das Schloss springen muss. Nervig.

Das an sich wär nicht schlimm.
Der größte Minuspunkt sind diverse Bosse. Diese sind generell eigentlich gut gemacht. Jeder unterschiedlich, mit eigenen Skills und eigenen Belohnungen.

Leider gibt es vereinzelt Bosse die so unfair sind, dass man, wenn man alleine Spielt, sehr große Mühen hat diese zu bezwingen. Da ist der Boss definitiv falsch gebalanced, denn die 3 Bosse davor und danach sind zwar auch schwer, aber mit 1-3 Anläufen erledigt. Selbst, wenn man 2 Level drunter ist.
Da hilft auch der Blutmond, höchst-mögliches Gear, maximum an Tränken und Elixieren und selbst die Erhöhung des Schadens auf das 3-fache in den Optionen nichts. Gar nichts! Auch alles zusammen nicht.

Den Boss juckt das nicht, der eskaliert fröhlich, spawnt 10 Mobs, die verlangsamen einen, man kann nicht weg und die prügeln einen in 1,276 Sekunden tot, obwohl man bis dato perfekt ausgewichen ist. Das ist unteranderem daran geschuldet, dass einige Boss-Arenen, wenn vorhanden, beim Kammeraschwenk die Sicht blockieren. Ohne was zu sehen ist es schwer auszuweichen. 

Da ich ein Fan von davon bin, dass ein Spiel nicht stressiger als Arbeit seinen sollte, gibt es dafür einen Daumen runter. Schade.

V Rising é um ótimo jogo de rpg para quem quer aproveitar o tempo livre, seja sozinho ou com amigos. Sempre há algo para fazer, então é difícil ficar entediado.

O progresso é bastante legal, você coleta recursos, fabrica equipamentos e fortalece seu personagem para conseguir enfrentar diversos bosses, que lhes concede recompensas e desbloqueia novas skills, itens etc. Mesmo jogando sozinho, caso esteja em um servidor público, é comum encontrar jogadores dispostos a te ajudar, a comunidade é bem tranquila.

A construção de castelos é outro ponto forte. O jogo oferece uma boa variedade de opções de decoração e personalização, especialmente para quem possui as DLCs, o que é impressionante considerando que esse não é o foco principal do jogo. A personalização do personagem é relativamente simples, mas cumpre bem o seu papel.

Além desses pontos, o jogo possui muitas outras qualidades que você pode descobrir jogando ou assistindo vídeos de gameplay.

Ele costuma entrar em promoção por cerca de R$30 a R$50, se você tem interesse no gênero, vale muito a pena dar uma chance.

Well, giving negative review to this game seems almost unfair since there is a lot of quality and charm in this epic vampire power fantasy. ARPG-style gameplay is fun, tons of weapons and different combos/skills, environments and monsters are unique and varied, vampire castles can be designed to your heart's content. I like that you can switch to any weapon at any point and rebind skills to try out different playstyles. Combat is tight with some boss fights really well designed requiring to learn enemy movesets, gimmicks or counters.

However ultimately this game does not respect your time with annoying, limiting mechanics - fighting and traveling during the day is often impossible (good luck when sun comes up during a boss fight in an open field), teleporting with majority of items is forbidden (making a teleporter a one-way really because as soon as you loot anything you cannot teleport back), traversal through enormous map takes forever (even though running as a wolf is fun first few hours). In that respect, game is similar to vanilla Valheim. If that is something that does not turn you off - you will probably like V Rising.

Where the game falls short is its very limited options for gear generally and gear progression overall, a very grindy / RNG experience to build and customize the weapons you want and skills you want to augment, and the fact that a core mechanism for customizing your weapons and gem augmentations does not come until what feels like the end of the game's PvE progression. A great game overall and worth the buy at any price if you're in it for the PvP, and probably on sale if you're only going to play for PvE.

Very underrated game in its genre. Here are my pros and cons for V Rising:


POSITIVE:

- The combat is fluid, responsive, and skill-based, quite similar to League of Legends abilities. You have skillshots, aoe spells, ultimates, summons, effects, etc. You have a weapon which grants you a basic attack + 2 weapon abilities, and 3 spells that you can chose from various schools (2 base spells and 1 ultimate). While quite simple, you can mix and match a lot and obtain different builds.

- The open world feels alive. There are different factions that have towns, settlements, and are roaming around. Of course (almost) everyone is hostile to you, however factions may fight between them. It is also possible for roaming bosses of different factions to fight each other, leading to some funny cheese moments.

- The whole vampire/blood/shapeshifting mechanics are great. The blood system is super interesting and allows for different strengths. You can also turn into wolf/bear/rat/bat/etc, unlocked by bosses and each form having its own utility (mainly outside of combat).

- The base building is nice, being very simple but allowing for some nice designs.


NEGATIVE:

- The grind is a bit tedious at some parts, however the game has the option to modify this by reducing craft times, increasing loot, etc.

- Brutal difficulty is very hard when playing solo, however not impossible. A lot of bosses can be beaten by cheesing them, however without cheesing some have BS abilities that one shot you or summon annoying minions that distract your fight. However this is also a skill issue...

- The camera rotating management needs some time to get used to


Other than that absolute banger of a game, for under 20 bucks this is a steal for the content you get!

[h1]V Rising: A Gothic Masterpiece of Survival and Action Combat[/h1]

[i]V Rising is a phenomenal achievement in the survival genre, masterfully blending top-down action-RPG combat with deep base building and vampire lore. Developed by Stunlock Studios, this game successfully avoids the typical survival pitfalls by making you feel like a powerful predator reclaiming your empire, rather than just another weakling trying to stay alive. With its fluid mechanics, rich atmosphere, and highly rewarding progression, it stands as an absolute must-play for fans of both survival games and action RPGs alike.[/i]

[h2]🧛 The Vampire Power Fantasy and Atmosphere[/h2]
The atmosphere in V Rising is brilliantly dark and gothic. From the sun-dappled forests to the grim, foggy farmlands and cursed woods, the world feels incredibly alive and dangerous. What makes the game truly stand out is how it forces you to adapt to being a vampire: the sun is your absolute enemy, and navigating the shadows during the daytime turns simple travel into a tense, thrilling puzzle. The visual style is crisp and stylized, perfectly capturing the moody, blood-soaked aesthetic of a dark fantasy realm.

[h2]⚔️ Combat and Blood Types[/h2]
Combat is heavily inspired by Stunlock's previous arena-shooter pedigree, meaning it is fast, fluid, and completely skill-based. Utilizing a mix of directional skill-shots, dashes, and weapon abilities, every encounter feels incredibly engaging. The "Blood Type" system is a stroke of pure genius. Feeding on different targets—like a rogue, a brute, or a worker—grants you unique, dynamic buffs based on the quality of their blood. This turns hunting into a strategic choice, as you actively scout for the perfect prey to boost your specific playstyle.

[h2]🏰 Castle Building and Raiding[/h2]
The base-building mechanic is exceptionally rewarding. Instead of just throwing together a simple wooden shack, you erect a massive, multi-floor gothic castle complete with grand pillars, blood fountains, and production workshops. Watching your domain grow from a small coffin in the woods into a sprawling fortress is intensely satisfying. Managing your territory, defending it from rival players (on PvP servers), and commanding your own vampire servants to gather resources gives you the genuine feeling of being a dark lord ruling over the land.

[h2]⚠️ Drawbacks[/h2]
While the game is incredibly polished, the resource grind can become quite intensive, especially in the late-game stages where crafting top-tier gear requires massive amounts of rare materials. For solo players on public servers, progression can feel significantly slower and punishing if caught in the crosshairs of larger clans. Additionally, the progression relies heavily on defeating specific V Blood bosses, which can occasionally feel like a rigid checklist rather than organic exploration. However, these factors take very little away from the stellar core loop.

[h2]🏆 Conclusion[/h2]
V Rising is a shining example of how to perfectly execute an early-access-to-full-release journey. It successfully combines the tactical depth of an ARPG with the addictive loop of a survival builder, wrapped in an unforgettable vampire fantasy.

Whether you are dodging sunbeams, hunting powerful bosses for their magical abilities, or expanding the walls of your majestic castle, the game offers hundreds of hours of high-quality entertainment. It is an incredibly rewarding indie titan that deserves a permanent spot in your collection.

[h3]Rating: 9.5/10[/h3]

El combate y la ambientación son excelentes, pero todo termina sepultado por un grindeo exagerado. El juego parece diseñado para estirar artificialmente cada progreso: farmear recursos durante horas, esperar tiempos de fabricación, recorrer enormes distancias para conseguir materiales específicos y repetir el mismo ciclo una y otra vez.
Lo peor es que muchas veces no sentís que estés avanzando por habilidad o estrategia, sino simplemente porque invertiste suficientes horas haciendo tareas repetitivas. Si morís, perdés tiempo. Si necesitás mejorar el equipo, perdés tiempo. Si querés construir el castillo, perdés tiempo recolectando miles de materiales. Todo parece pensado para alargar la experiencia en lugar de hacerla más divertida.

Entiendo que el grindeo forma parte del género de supervivencia, pero acá se siente excesivo y termina convirtiéndose en un trabajo. En vez de tener ganas de jugar "una partida más", terminás pensando en todo lo que vas a tener que farmear antes de poder hacer algo realmente interesante.

Tiene muy buenas ideas, una estética increíble y un sistema de combate que engancha, pero el ritmo del progreso termina arruinando la experiencia. Si tenés poco tiempo para jugar, probablemente pases más horas haciendo tareas repetitivas que disfrutando del contenido.

No lo recomiendo, salvo que disfrutes de los juegos donde el grindeo constante sea el objetivo principal.

接着就是缺点。第一也是最影响游戏体验的，角色的移速太慢了。这极大地影响了我的游戏体验。跑图是一方面，更糟糕的是BOSS战。BOSS战中充满了很多弹幕攻击，而玩家操控的角色移速之慢，使得躲弹幕很多时候必须背板，因为根本没法凭反应来躲，移速太慢了。 
以上是第一点，移速。第二点则可以与第一点放在一起看。游戏的战斗是一大特色，先前也说了，移速很慢，然而通用的位移技能却又只有一个，且CD长达8秒多。我只能说，战斗体验很普通、很一般。
第三点实际上也是延续了前两点所说的。角色不灵活意味着容易被打，然而这个游戏的战斗中回血手段及其匮乏，回的血非常少，真是一点点回的。本来游戏应该有血瓶类似的设计，这个游戏也有。但回血的药在战斗中效果受限，且被打就失效。

因此，说了这么多，总结一下，我想表达的就是，这个游戏的战斗部分体验绝对不算好，只能说是很一般。不过建筑部分还是很不错的。对于一款战斗建筑参半的游戏，我其实不是那么满意，战斗比起建筑部分来说差得多了。
还算是值得一玩，最好要有朋友，我是跟别人双人玩的，我觉得单人玩会挺无趣的。

This game is just Rust but with vampires and additional poor game design decisions.

1. The blueprint system is functionally identical to Rust. It takes hours of real world to time get materials as environmental hazards that do multiple times the amount of damage to you and more heavily geared players target you for those materials. It then takes hours of real world time to craft the blueprints to get higher level equipment. There is also a massive debuff inflicted upon you where you do a small fraction of the damage you should be doing to anything that is a higher level than you, which is obnoxious and makes it effectively impossible to skip the grind using skill.
2. Walking anywhere is incredibly annoying because of how slowly you move, at least at the start. Walk for 15 minutes to go kill a boss that unlocks a skill, die to a random enemy on the way that can kill you in 1/40th the amount of hits that it takes you to kill it despite the boss being half it's level, then have to walk all the way back. The boss was literally easier than a random enemy that spawned next to it from my 2 hours of gameplay. This is poor game design.
3. Real world time based systems ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SUCKS ON PC. I do not have 40+ hours per week to play this game and I am not going to make the time. I dont want to check the game every 4 hours every day for weeks just to be able to progress. The UI in the settings for a lot of these options was apparently removed in a previous update, which is a critically poor decision for game design. The UI also only allows you to set most fields to 6x speed, which still means youre waiting for 15 minutes to craft stuff a lot of the time. 
There is a .json file that can be modified, which I did, to set everything to higher speeds, but even that is missing many of the fields like research speed. I have little faith in any game devs that decide to remove options from the server side settings like this for no apparent reason as it disables players from deciding how they want to play the game.

 Но тем не менее игрушка очень приятная, Механика строительства прикольная. отстраивать свой замок можно весьма креативно и красиво, сделано это всё просто так что процесс не вгоняет в уныние, крафт всяких штук и добыча ресурсов тоже интересные, гринд в игре в принципе приятный, но при большом НО! [h1]The Gameplay: [/h1]
Build a bunch of stuff, but with a solid gathering and combat mechanics. Your strength is entirely determined by your gear and there is no experience or skill tree that muddies that, instead you kill bosses to make progress on your character. So killing 2000 enemies only gets 2000 enemies worth of material, no strength or anything like that. But killing a boss will allow you to now craft better armor or refineries etc. It's an odd, but still very enjoyable gameplay loop. 

[h1]The Story:[/h1]
It isn't really prominent, most of it is environmental story telling which does a good job here. It's not completely bare-bones and the bosses/enemies etc have a very thoughtful placement that tells a story of it's own. There is also your self-made story on how you go about this which is open ended. This is not my favorite style but again it got the job done and it hit the parts that mattered to make it enjoyable for me.

[h1]The Visuals:[/h1]
This game has a lot of confidence and charisma in their art. They know how to give you and your castle good drip. The attacks, the gestures, the style of the environment and enemies all are a delight for the eyes in a well done cartoonish style. Each area has it's own look and feel, and they look and feel great.

[h1]The Sound:[/h1]
This game had a big sound budget, and you can tell. It gets carries it hard, from the sound effects of combat to the music. which are all powerful in their own right. However the voice acting of each an every boss, or your character trumps all that. It really makes fighting each boss unique and anything you do that involves your character talking that much better.

[h1]The Experience:[/h1]
This game reminds me of Tribes of Midgard at first, which also had mechanics were just as weird. However, this game set itself apart with the theme and attention to detail on the small things. I found myself really loving this game whereas I couldn't wait to get off of Tribes. There was love and hella craft put into this game and then you add in the castlvania cross over too... oomf, so good. It's an easy recommend in my book and I can see myself playing it long after I already 100%ed it.

Esta experiencia destaca por la distribución del juego, el poder ayudarte con compañeros puede reducir el farmeo y permitirte builds más libres como jugador al tener compañeros que puedan permitirte curarte.

JUEGUEN ESTE JUEGO ALOJANDO USTEDES SU SERVER

Lo mas negativo de este juego es su trecho final, se siente incompleto. El nivel maximo es 91, se centra demasiado en el PvP al punto que pasivas que dan cosas como mayor velocidad usando algo como las transformaciones de vampiro (cosas que no son viables en combate) se volvieron algo elegible para una casilla. V Rising looks like another survival crafting game, but Stunlock Studios managed to create something much more unique: a vampire action RPG where every system perfectly supports the fantasy of becoming a powerful creature of the night.

The gameplay loop is incredibly addictive: explore Vardoran, hunt powerful enemies, absorb their blood to unlock new abilities, improve your gear, and build your own gothic castle. Every upgrade feels meaningful, and progression constantly gives you a new reason to venture further into the world.

The combat is where the game truly shines. Fast, responsive, and skill-based, it feels closer to an action RPG or even a competitive arena game than a traditional survival title. Boss fights are varied, satisfying, and require you to actually learn patterns, dodge attacks, and adapt your build.

The castle building is also a fantastic addition. Creating your own vampire fortress, decorating it, and slowly transforming a ruined hideout into a true dark kingdom is incredibly rewarding.

And while the game is already great solo, V Rising is definitely better in co-op. Playing with friends completely enhances the experience: you can share resources, build your castle together, specialize your characters, and take down powerful bosses as a vampire clan. This is where the fantasy really comes alive.

After its early access period and its 1.0 release, V Rising feels like a game made with a clear vision and a lot of passion.

If you enjoy survival games, action RPGs, or simply want to live your best vampire life, this one is absolutely worth your time.

V Rising : Enfin un jeu qui a du mordant et de la profondeur

Après avoir navigué dans des eaux bien troubles avec des titres sans intérêt, V Rising fait l'effet d'une véritable bouffée d'air frais (ou plutôt d'ombre fraîche). Ici, on sent immédiatement que les développeurs avaient une vision claire et, surtout, qu'ils respectent le temps et l'intelligence de leurs joueurs.

Une progression gratifiante
Ce qui marque d'emblée, c'est la structure. Contrairement à ces jeux "d'assistés" où tout est prémâché, V Rising demande de l'investissement. La gestion de votre château, la traque des boss pour débloquer de nouvelles capacités et la nécessité de jongler avec vos ressources créent une boucle de gameplay addictive et exigeante. On sent réellement une montée en puissance : vous commencez comme une proie vulnérable et finissez en véritable prédateur du monde de Vardoran. Chaque victoire sur un boss apporte un sentiment d'accomplissement bien réel, car il faut apprendre les mécaniques et préparer son coup.

Un univers cohérent et soigné
La direction artistique est remarquable. Le monde est sombre, immersif, et la mécanique de la lumière du soleil ajoute une tension constante qui force à réfléchir à ses déplacements et à sa stratégie. Ce n'est pas juste un jeu de survie de plus ; c'est un jeu qui a une identité forte, avec un gameplay nerveux et des systèmes de combat qui exigent un minimum de skill.

Enfin un jeu pour ceux qui veulent jouer, pas subir
C'est tout le contraire des expériences passives et creuses. V Rising vous demande de vous impliquer, de planifier et d'exécuter avec précision. Il y a une vraie satisfaction à bâtir son empire et à dominer les autres joueurs ou les menaces environnantes.

En résumé :
Si vous cherchez un jeu qui allie survie, stratégie et action pure, avec une profondeur qui justifie réellement d'y passer des dizaines d'heures, V Rising est une valeur sûre. C'est un titre solide, bien pensé, et qui prouve qu'on peut encore faire des jeux exigeants qui ne prennent pas le joueur pour un imbécile. Une excellente pioche.

Hello everyone, I want to show you the game from two sides.

The first side is solo play / playing on PvE servers with other people. For those who want to experience something new or explore a new game world, this is possibly one of the best games I can recommend to you. At the time of writing this review, character progression is built almost perfectly. The number of bosses doesn't make you feel bored. The PvE aspect alone can take anywhere from 20 to 60 hours, depending on whether or not you got caught up in the grand construction of a beautiful gothic castle.

The second side is PvP servers. Unfortunately, I can't say anything positive here, except for the interesting community. All you can experience or feel is pain.

Low new player traffic. Without addressing this point, any new player will find it difficult to even get started with minimal PvP, such as arena battles.

Everything good and related to PvP has been made by the players, not the developers. From this point, you get a simple piece of advice — whether you learn or not is up to you. New players ignore this and drop the game, and those who decide to push further end up facing points 1 and 3.

Anti-cheat. There isn't one. And there's no way for you to prove whether someone on your server is using cheats or not. Essentially, it's a blind game, and you might think, "That one player probably has 5,000 hours in the game and knows all the combos by heart and reads timings?" But it turns out it's just $20 wasted on a "Boost Your Skill" subscription.

And there is a point that ties all of this together — the developers have stopped adding new content. This is where all the previous problems stem from, as they are all interconnected. That's why I would not recommend buying this game. A developer should take care of their product, especially if it's an online project.

The game is good, don't get me wrong, but I'm struggling to recommend it.

It's got a lot of good gameplay, but then they follow it up with some really dumb design choices that make the game super frustrating to play.

As an example, there is NO WAY to turn off "Medium core", aka drop items on death. Now by default you don't drop your gear, so that's good, but by dropping the rest of your items on death, it means that if you die on a boss with anything on you (like consumable health potions to heal before re-engaging the boss) you're screwed. Now you have to pull the boss while on low health, then try and loot your ♥♥♥♥, then reset the fight.
This gets made all the worse if you decide to use the late-game amulets, which also drop on death. And because Item Level is everything, now you're 25 item levels lower than anything on the run back to the boss and will die in one or two hits. 

Speaking of Item Level, I think it's a really questionable system. I get the idea, it's a way to scale enemies while allowing for flexibility in gear. 
But in practice what it means is that later on in the game you settle on one weapon, because it becomes super expensive to have separate weapons, and if you ever switch off of that weapon, it'll lower your item level and you'll now take a lot more damage.

There's more, like the game being impossible to play with anything higher than 60 ping. I played with a friend on 120ms, and I had so many times where I was dodging abilities on my end, and then the game saying "no ♥♥♥♥ you, you got hit".


Anyway, if you're looking to play solo or with low latency, look at changing some server settings. Otherwise you're gonna be in for a bit of a rough time.

《夜族崛起》是我近期最上癮的生存建造遊戲之一，也是少數讓我願意一次又一次挑戰首領、順便把城堡蓋得越來越豪華的作品。

一開始只是衝著吸血鬼題材來玩，結果發現它幾乎把我喜歡的元素全都放進去了。你可以狩獵、採集、建造自己的城堡，也可以四處探索、討伐強大的 V 血首領。最棒的是，這些系統並不是各玩各的，而是緊密地串在一起：每打倒一位首領，都能獲得新的技能、建築或配方，讓人很清楚下一步該做什麼。那種「再打一個王就去睡」的想法，通常會讓你不知不覺又玩上好幾個小時。

遊戲的美術真的很對我的胃口。裝備和服裝設計既華麗又充滿哥德風格，尤其是披風和盔甲，換上新裝備的瞬間，戰力有沒有提升先不說，帥度絕對是直接拉滿。蓋好城堡之後，還會忍不住在大廳裡多站幾秒，欣賞自己的吸血鬼品味。

首領戰也是本作的一大亮點。每位王都有鮮明的特色和獨特機制，不是單純地堆數值，而是真的需要觀察節奏、學習走位。當然，學習的過程難免會伴隨著無數次倒地，但沒關係，難度其實很友善 死個億百次，總有一次會帥氣地把王收掉。當你終於打贏那個卡了好幾次的首領時，成就感真的非常高。

更難得的是，它對單人玩家也很友善。即使沒有固定的朋友一起玩，一個人也能按照自己的步調慢慢發展，今天專心蓋城堡，明天出去打王，完全不會覺得被進度追著跑。

總之，《夜族崛起》成功讓我實現了「白天躲在城堡睡覺、晚上出門工作（打王）」的吸血鬼夢想。如果你喜歡生存建造、動作戰鬥，或只是單純想當一位穿著帥氣披風、擁有豪華古堡的吸血鬼領主，這款遊戲真的非常值得一試。

V Rising – Strong Presentation and Fun Base Building, but Not Without Limits

V Rising presents itself very well, especially through its atmospheric gothic world and smooth gameplay loop. The game’s survival structure is easy to understand, and it quickly draws you into the role of a growing vampire lord. Exploration, combat, and progression all work together in a way that feels engaging and purposeful.

One of the most enjoyable parts is definitely the base building. It is simple, intuitive, and surprisingly satisfying. Placing structures, expanding your castle, and slowly turning it into a dark stronghold feels rewarding without ever becoming overly complicated. The system is streamlined, which makes it easy to get into even for players who usually don’t enjoy survival building mechanics.

At the same time, the game doesn’t go extremely deep in its systems. Some players may find that long-term complexity and variety could be higher, especially in the late game where progression can feel a bit repetitive. Still, the overall experience remains solid and enjoyable, especially for shorter or medium play sessions.

Overall, V Rising delivers a strong and stylish survival experience with a particularly enjoyable base building system, even if it doesn’t fully push the genre forward in every area.

V Rising – Starke Präsentation und cooler Basenbau, aber nicht ohne Grenzen

V Rising macht insgesamt einen sehr guten ersten Eindruck, vor allem durch die düstere, atmosphärische Spielwelt und den angenehm flüssigen Gameplay-Loop. Das Survival-System ist leicht verständlich und zieht einen schnell in die Rolle eines aufstrebenden Vampirherrschers hinein. Erkundung, Kämpfe und Fortschritt greifen gut ineinander und wirken motivierend.

Besonders positiv fällt der Basenbau auf. Er ist simpel, intuitiv und überraschend befriedigend. Gebäude platzieren, das eigene Schloss erweitern und Schritt für Schritt eine dunkle Festung aufbauen fühlt sich lohnend an, ohne jemals überkompliziert zu werden. Das System ist bewusst zugänglich gehalten, was auch Spieler anspricht, die sonst eher wenig mit Survival-Bau anfangen können.

Gleichzeitig bleibt das Spiel in manchen Bereichen eher auf der einfachen Seite. Vor allem im späteren Verlauf könnte etwas mehr Tiefe und Abwechslung gut tun, da sich der Fortschritt teilweise wiederholen kann. Trotzdem bleibt das Gesamterlebnis stabil und unterhaltsam, besonders für kürzere oder mittlere Spielsessions.

Insgesamt bietet V Rising ein starkes, stilvolles Survival-Erlebnis mit einem sehr gelungenen Basenbau, auch wenn es nicht in jedem Bereich neue Maßstäbe setzt.

1. Разнообразие билдов через разные школы магии и множество пушек разной степени полезности.
2. Уникальная прогрессия через убийство боссов и сбор различных типов крови с уникальными эффектами.
3. Достаточно разнообразный ростер боссов
4. Система слуг и оффлайн фарм ресурсов через них.
5. Огромное сборище отсылок и референсов на монстров и непосредственно вампиров из попкультуры
6. Шикарный артдизайн и готический стиль
К минусам игры можно отнести следующие вещи:
1. Атаки врагов подвержены пингу даже если вы играете в одиночку
2. Невозможность телепортации некоторых ресурсов даже на PVE или одиночном сервере
3. Ближе к концу игры у некоторых боссов слегка перекручена сложность (проходил на Жестокой)
4. Фарм всего от материалов и расходников до слуг и модификаторов оружия и заклинаний
По итогу хочется сказать, что для меня плюсы игры перевешиваю минусы, большая часть из которых является либо придирками, либо вещами, которые 90% игроков не прочувствуют. Рекомендую.

Au début je me disais "encore un jeu de type Craft mais en vue de dessus ...." mais non, V Rising c'est plus que cela, même si on y joue simplement en solo. Le côté craft n'est ni novateur, ni mauvais et fonctionne très bien, c'est propre, clair et fonctionnel, c'est ce qu'on demande. le côté action est, quant à lui, plu complexe que je le pensais, il ne suffit pas de frapper les ennemis sans réfléchir, non. Plus on progresse, plus le jeu introduit de nouvelle mécanique qu'il faut exploiter pour progresser plus efficacement. 
Pour moi c'est une vraie surprise et je recommande ce jeu à toute personne cherchant une alternative un peu plus basé action et objectifs à réalisé par rapport à des jeux de survie/craft plus classiques.

Спустя 52 часа игра пройдена на 100% достижений с нуля. Это были прекрасные 52 часа в дуо со своими радостными и рейдж моментами. И хочу поделиться немного своим мнением на счет этой игры.
[h2]Строительство:[/h2]
В игре прекрасно сделана механика строительства замка, ведь ты можешь поставить его на любом выделенном участке по ВСЕЙ карте. Ты сам определяешь размер замка, комнат, как они выглядят ,где что находится и это рай для любителей стройки (можно хоть башню Арасака построить)
[h2]Фарм ресурсов:[/h2]
Гринд в игре не чувствуется ,нет ощущения ,что тебя душат, пока ты обегаешь половину карты и фармишь. Зачастую достаточно добыть 5-10 стаков одного ресурса и тебе его хватит почти до конца игры. Возможно ,возникает вопрос: "А разве добывать 10 стаков одного и того же ресурса , так еще и зачастую бежать по полтора километра до замка без возможности телепортироваться с ресурсами - это не душка?"
И лично мой ответ :"Нет!"
Карта хоть и огромная ,но имеет хорошее наполнение ,атмосферу и свою красоту в каждой из локаций ,так что все пробежки приносят только удовольствие.
[h2]Боссы:[/h2]
Боссы сделаны балансно ,каждый запоминается свой стилистикой ,цветовой гаммой, тем, как выглядят атаки и какие реплики они произносят во время битвы.
За всю игру были проблемы только с двумя боссами: [spoiler] Адам Перерожденный и Бессмертный Король Дракула.[/spoiler]
([spoiler] Как же весело бить лицо Дракуле в его третьей стадии, когда переживаешь, что тебе опять не хватит полсекунды до конца перезарядки завесы или щита, и ты умрешь ,оставив ему 10% хп[/spoiler])
Хоть Vrising и напоминает по большей части соулс игры во время битв ,но тут не требуется делать по 100+ траев, чтобы просто запомнить мувсет босса. Зачастую на третий-четвертый трай уже можно спокойно доджить каждую атаку.
[h2]Механика крови:[/h2]
Играем за вампиров ,а что нужно вампирам для выживания? Правильно - кровь. И здесь это сделано крайне интересно ,ты не просто высасываешь каждого встречного ,чтобы увеличить свою силу, а занимаешься "селекцией" жертв, выискивая   лучшего, с самой чистой кровью для получения максимальных баффов.
Также хочется отметить ,что в игре присутствует кровь для любого стиля игры, вы 100% сможете найти свою любимую, с которой комфортнее всего играть в вашем темпе, она даже может кратно облегчит фарм. ([spoiler] К концу игры открывается возможность смешивать кровь, что делает механику крови еще более гибкой.[/spoiler])
[h2]Заключение:[/h2]
Vrising - это уникальная игра ,совмещающая в себе кучу разных ,а главное интересных механик и фич,  эта игра точно стоит вашего внимания и времени вне зависимости от того какой вы игрок: казул, хардкрорщик, любитель что либо построить, или чисто подраться с боссами, да вычистить пару поселений NPC. Всем найдется чем заняться в этой игре.

I really wanted to enjoy V Rising because the game itself has a lot going for it. The visuals, combat, progression, and survival mechanics are all excellent. Unfortunately, the controller implementation completely overshadowed those strengths for me.

My biggest issue is the camera controls. The default controller scheme requires continuously holding L2 to freely rotate the camera. I don't mind isometric games at all, I actually enjoy them, but this is one of the most uncomfortable controller schemes I've experienced. Constantly holding a trigger while moving, fighting, dodging, and managing abilities quickly became frustrating and unnecessarily fatiguing.

Before deciding to leave this review, I spent a good amount of time trying to solve the problem with Steam Input. I tested custom configurations and community layouts, expecting to remap the controls into something that felt more natural. None of them achieved the result I was looking for. From my experience, the game's controller implementation limits what Steam Input can do with the camera controls, leaving the default behavior essentially unchanged.

This isn't a complaint from someone who gave up after a few minutes. I genuinely wanted to make the game work on controller and invested the time trying to fix what I considered its biggest flaw. Unfortunately, after exhausting every solution I could find, I came to the conclusion that this is simply how the controller support is designed.

For me, the camera controls were a major drawback that prevented me from enjoying an otherwise excellent game. If the developers ever add native options for more conventional camera controls or allow greater customization, I'd gladly revisit my recommendation.

Until then, I can't recommend V Rising based on my experience as a controller first player.

V Rising is an outstanding survival crafting experience.

The combat feels fantastic from beginning to end. It's responsive, satisfying, and offers a huge amount of build variety through different weapons, spells, passives, and jewel modifications. Every V Blood boss feels unique and requires a different approach, making each victory rewarding. We played on Brutal difficulty, which was challenging without ever feeling unfair. Learning boss mechanics and improving over time made every encounter satisfying. It's also fun when roaming bosses unexpectedly run into each other and start fighting.

Castle building is another standout feature. The building system is intuitive and easy to use, and I really enjoyed designing, decorating, and continuously expanding my castle. New crafting stations, decorations, and upgrades keep unlocking throughout the game, giving you plenty of reasons to keep improving your base.

Exploration is consistently rewarding. Every region has its own distinct atmosphere, enemies, resources, and bosses, so there's always something new to discover.

Progression is excellent. Unlocking new abilities, crafting stations, and recipes through boss kills and research always feels meaningful. I expected the game to be much grindier than it actually was. Gathering resources can occasionally become a little repetitive, but it never felt excessive.

I had previously played the game solo and never finished it, but this time I experienced it with two friends in PvE, which made the game even more enjoyable. We skipped PvP entirely, and for us that was the right choice.

Visually, the game looks great. The gothic art style, music, and sound design all work together to create a fantastic vampire atmosphere. The gameplay is clearly the main focus rather than the story, and that's exactly where the game excels.

The game is quite long but never overstays its welcome because there's always another meaningful goal to work towards.

Performance was flawless during my playthrough. I didn't experience any bugs or technical issues.

Overall, V Rising is an outstanding survival game with excellent combat, rewarding progression, satisfying base building, and a world that's genuinely fun to explore. Highly recommended.

I have fallen in love with this game so much!

My S.O. and I like to spend time together later in the day playing whatever multiplayer game we can get our hands on. We typically play through a game (or at least a good portion of one) before moving on to the next or getting distracted by something else. It's usually the second. One day he mentioned trying V Rising. At first I wasn't sure, but over time the idea grew on me, especially since it looked fun and fit with my recent aesthetic interests.

V Rising is a survival RPG where you play as a vampire, roaming the world, drinking blood, climbing the ladder of bosses, and eventually facing Dracula himself... and that's really all it is! Somehow, though, I fell in love with it. It even became my own cozy game. It definitely isn't a cozy game by design, but it became one for me.

You can build your own castle and gardens, transform into different animals, explore a variety of biomes, and place your castle almost anywhere you want. You can play in your own private world, open it up to the public, or simply share it with a friend.

Interested?
~~~~

• Art/Graphics

The art is pretty good. It reminds me of many modern games with a similarly smooth, stylized look, such as Fortnite. However, V Rising uses that style in a way that perfectly suits its darker theme. The world is filled with rich, realistic color palettes that give everything a gothic atmosphere.

The textures especially shine when you're building your castle, and oh my... the castles are gorgeous. You can create almost anything you can imagine, and the building system lets you achieve an incredibly high level of gothic elegance.

The animal forms are always fun, and the wolf form is surprisingly adorable despite the simple art style. If the visuals aren't what you expected at first, trust me, they grow on you. The game manages to feel sleek, clean, and fast-paced while also being detailed and atmospheric, which works wonderfully with its top-down perspective.

It's a beautiful game, and the lighting is absolutely top-tier for me.

• Music

Originally, the music didn't stand out much to me. I wasn't expecting anything on the level of Castlevania, but it initially felt fairly simple.

Over time, though just like the art, it really grew on me. The soundtrack feels mysterious, subtle, and ambient. There were plenty of moments where I'd simply wander through a forest biome, listening to the quiet strings alongside the sounds of nature.

It feels dark and haunting while also being oddly comforting. It really captures the feeling of being a vampire, making me think about both how powerful and how lonely they can be. (It reminded me a lot of Alucard from Castlevania.)

• Gameplay/Mechanics

The gameplay flows beautifully.

As mentioned before, this is a survival RPG, but it also plays from a top-down perspective. When you're venturing outside your castle to hunt, gather resources, or defeat bosses, it almost feels like a Diablo-style game. You're constantly collecting materials to bring home and craft into new equipment and structures.

Combat is where the game really shines. It's fast-paced, responsive, and incredibly satisfying. Unlike Diablo, however, movement is done entirely with WASD while aiming and attacking with your mouse. At first this feels a little unusual, but it quickly becomes second nature.

Your main abilities are mapped to Spacebar, Q, and R, and boss fights can become incredibly intense. There are plenty of moments where your adrenaline spikes because you're constantly dodging attacks and making split-second decisions.

There are also many different weapons to suit your preferred playstyle. The Sword, Axe, Mace, and Spear each serve different combat purposes while also excelling at gathering specific resources. Axes chop trees efficiently, Maces are best for mining, and Spears deal extra damage to creatures. As you progress, you'll eventually unlock bows and even dual pistols, giving combat even more variety.

• Magic

Alongside the weapon system is an excellent magic system.

Every boss you defeat unlocks new crafting recipes, equipment, and magical abilities. There are schools of Blood, Fire, Frost, Necromancy, Illusion, and Storm magic (along with passive abilities). They're called different names in-game, but that's essentially what they represent.

You can only equip four abilities at once, so you'll need to think about how you want to build your character. Whether you prefer charging headfirst into combat, chaining together fast combos, or staying at a distance while supporting yourself with ranged spells, there's plenty of freedom to experiment.

• UI/HUD

The UI takes a little getting used to. There are a lot of menus assigned to different keys, and remembering what each one does can be confusing at first. K opens the V Blood menu, J opens your spellbook, B enters building mode, Tab opens your character menu, and so on.

Once you get used to it, though, it all feels very intuitive.

The HUD itself is clean and unobtrusive. Your current objectives stay tucked away in the top-left corner instead of constantly demanding your attention. Aside from your minimap, the day/night clock, your abilities, and your blood meter, very little clutters the screen.

• Overall

This game has grown on me so much, and I absolutely love it.

It took a little while, but the combination of the art, music, and gameplay creates an atmosphere that genuinely feels like living as a vampire. If you enjoy top-down action RPGs or Diablo-style gameplay, I think you'll really enjoy V Rising.

It has an atmosphere that I haven't really found in another game. Even compared to something like Vampire: The Masquerade, V Rising feels unique. Playing it has also made me even more excited for Dawn of the Bloodwalker.

For me, it's become a relaxing comfort game. It's incredibly easy to boot up, spend a few hours building a castle, gather resources, defeat a boss or two, and log off feeling satisfied. Unlike many survival games, it never feels overly stressful. Aside from managing your blood supply, most of your time is spent building your castle and progressing through the game's excellent boss system.

Overall, I give V Rising a **9.2/10**.

I'd love to see another game capture this same feeling but in third-person with even more detailed graphics. Until then, this has become my personal favorite vampire experience, and I'll happily continue spending hours building more castles.

V Rising is an awesome game that lets you build cool castles, experiment with different builds and live out a vampire fantasy, it unfortunately loses steam about halfway through when it comes to unlocking new types of builds or designs for your castle. This sucks because before that it has a really good sense of progression where you can do a couple of bosses, go back to your castle to upgrade it, gather resources, craft new armor and weapons and repeat. After that however you kind of stop unlocking things that really make you go back and spend some time in your castle or gather resources so it mostly becomes a boss rush for the second half, this however does not hold the game back from being great.

It can however be quite tricky to 100%, The toughest achievements are definitely gonna be A Perfect Test Subject, which has you feeding a prisoner Irradiant Gruel and have them reach 100% blood quality. Irradiant gruel has a 65% chance to improve the prisoners blood quality by 1-2% but also a 35% chance of transforming them into a mutant. It really just comes down to RNG and having a prisoner that is preferably already at 99% blood quality.

Other than that most achievements are fairly straightforward where if you simply play the game you will unlock most of them, however as I said you need to complete the game on Brutal. This is the sole reason as to why the difficulty rating is hard as especially Dracula is a tough boss. I personally did it together with 2 other friends, supposedly it can be somewhat easier solo and you might even be able to trivialize the fight via the modified settings. All in all good luck, Dracula is tough.

[h2]Played it on brutal/100+ Hours on first playthrough/100% Completed. I more than got my moneys worth and then some. [/h2]


I had been wanting to scratch a vampire itch for awhile now and have always been on the fence about this game. The appeal of facing tons of bosses, building my own castle, and slowly but surely becoming the number 1 vampire was so alluring.

[b]PVE, PVP, or SOLO?[/b] - I played on a PVE sever, so no fighting other players. Which, if all you want to focus on is the bosses and castle building, then this is the way to play. So you dont have to worry about others destroying your castle that you spent hours on. Because once its gone, you gotta start from scratch. The community of players I saw, out in the wild, are super friendly and helpful. At this point in the games life, they are mostly people who have already completed the game several times and are just helping others with bosses. So if you need help, especially late game, they will help.

I hear PVP servers can be super sweaty, and very difficult for new players. So play at your own discretion.

[b]Castle Building[/b] - was awesome! Keeping in mind, you wont have the coolest things at first, but certain bosses you defeat allow you to craft cooler and cooler things for your castle as the game progresses. From, different lighting options(with several colors), to wallpaper to change up your castles look, flooring, decorations etc...,,you can literally make your ideal castle. Designing each room with different lighting and decorations really made the place feel alive, especially with your servants walking around. I spent so many hours building my castle the way i wanted.

[b]Progression[/b] - can feel a little slow. On normal, your usually on an even playing field with the enemies, but on brutal they are typically like 3 lvls above you. So for combat on brutal, its alot of trial and error. Constantly running back to finish the job or pick up your gear. Gathering enough materials can take a bit too, but luckly if your playing in your own server, you can tweak those setting and get material faster.

[b]Boss Fights[/b] - good depending on who you ask. Each boss has their own cool design, attack, or gimmick. Like diablo or PoE. They can certainly have a learning curve to them. So optimizing your spells and weapons are a must on brutal. Towards the end game, i did have some help, from other players on the server, for the final boss. It was awesome, their was like 6 or 7 of us all fighting [spoiler]Dracula.[/spoiler] It wasn't easy, we failed dozens of times, due to his scailling with more players. But in the end, we got it done and it felt like i was raiding in an MMO, it was a highlight of this game for me.

[b]My only gripes are small nitpicks:[/b]
- Your walking speed in crazy slow. A chunk of gameplay is the dreaded walk back to your gear or boss, once youv'e been killed.
- Needed more character customization options. The character creation is rather lacking. Wish it was more fleshed out to build my ideal vampire.
- If you play on a PVP or PVE server, expect not many plots of land to build your castle. The ideal/bigger plots of land are likely already taken. You wont have to worry about this if your playing on your on solo server.
- TRISTAN THE VAMPIRE HUNTER....F YOU. WHY ARE YOU A FREE ROAMING BOSS IN THE STARTING ZONE AHHHHHHHHHHHHH.

[b]Biggest Positive:[/b]
Shout out to that one castle who had a loaded flower garden for anyone to gather (to use for crafting gear/potions). So helpful. You are the real MVP of this game.

[b]Overall 9/10 game.[/b] If i had more time,  i would have stretched this game out longer because of how fun it is. But i paid $7 for this, and i got MORE than my moneys worth of it. [b]Highly Recommend.[/b]

Well, it has released, and I have now tried it. And it is great!
I can go at length about how the building works, or make quirky jokes or whatever, but frankly I'll just say it's an overall great experience with lovely callbacks to their previous games and a great mix of OWSC with action and vampires. And the DLCs are all cosmetic and entirely optional. They are overpriced imho, but if you can afford them - definitely worth picking up to support SLS for the great work they've done on the game, while also getting yourself more customization option for your vampire and their castle(s)!
I've picked up all the DLCs myself now, after spending about 50ish hours in this game, enjoying just about every moment of it!
In terms of what sort of game to expect - it's kind of like Terraria in the sense of progress being bound to killing the next boss, so it has a linear combat-focused progression, and that's one of the main gameplay loops, along with basebuilding and farming resources, and exploring the world and the game's features. On that last part, I must say, the game's quite intuitive, for the most part. As is the basebuilding system.
The only complaint I've found myself to have are some things I find to be oddities and a bit nonsensical, primarily about controls (keybinds, options, etc.) but you get used to it. 

Overall, great game if you love OWSC + Vampires + Action combat

The base building and castle siege mechanics were very fun to play around with, and I remember fondly as I conquered an enemy castle like a medieval king coming to claim his rightful place against the plebeians who dare reach above their station. Some of the later boss fights, but especially the last 4, felt like high level raid bosses in an MMO, with a lot of dodging, bobbing and weaving, as well as perfect timing necessary to survive the encounter. Fantastic game all round, fun gameplay, really strong theming, great designs for everything from enemies and weapons to basic foliage and junk in settlements that help the game feel alive, lots of really nice quality of life stuff and really well polished. 

The base building is really fun and rewarding, and the ability to relocate and rebuild easily is such an amazing quality of life mechanic as you progress into new areas.

The resource gathering does get quite grindy towards the end but the thrall system is a fun little addition to alleviate that burden.

The gameplay is very satisfying with lots of different playstyles available between all the weapons and schools of magic, and the game does a really good job of starting you off feeling pretty pathetic and weak, and slowly building you up until you are super strong, and the best part is it really feels like you earned it.

I was a bit thrown off by the wow style controls but with your character always facing the cursor, but you get used to it fairly quickly.

The V blood bosses unlocking the tech to help you grow stronger works way better than I expected, it means you cant out gear bosses and need to learn patterns and adjust your weapons/buffs to suit the bosses. 

The actual fight design is a bit hit or miss, most of them are fantastic, fun and the right level of challenging. 
Some are kind of boring and unfun, the final boss thankfully is really hard but fun and rewarding once you figure it out!

If you're looking for a vampire themed survival game, V Rising delivers a very good multiplayer experience. I highly recommend playing it with other people, as the game is primarily focused on the PvP aspect. That said, you can also enjoy it as a pure PvE game on your own private server. Solo play is viable too, it's just more grindy, and you'll be missing out on the main aspect of the game.
The soundtrack is pleasantly chill, setting a relaxed atmosphere that fits the gothic aesthetic well. One of the game's strongest features is the wide range of settings available. You can customize the game completely to your liking. If you're the type of player who likes to relax and doesn't want to deal with stressful boss fights, you can go down that road. On the flip side, if you enjoy a serious challenge and heavy grinding, you can adjust the settings accordingly and feel right at home.
The ability system seems fairly simple and it is. If you're someone who loves spending dozens of hours experimenting and creating crazy, nonsensical builds, this won't be your thing. The game follows the philosophy that simplicity is beauty. The system is clear, easy to understand, and very straightforward in its progression. Even players with no RPG experience will feel right at home. 
The level design is nicely varied, with distinct biomes like dark forests, snowy peaks, and cursed swamps. Each area has its own feel and enemy types, which keeps exploration engaging.
The progression system might rub some people the wrong way. Personally, it's not my cup of tea, but I can endure it. I can understand that the "go here, kill this, and this unlocks for you" style can feel clunky and even annoying to some players.
Building your castle is intuitive and fun. The grid system keeps everything tidy, and there are plenty of cosmetic options to make your lair look great. Overall, it's a solid and satisfying system that adds a lot to the game. Optimization is solid overall. The game runs smoothly and I didn't run into any serious bugs or crashes.
Now, about the boss fights and overall difficulty. We played on the hardest difficulty, and I have to say that the boss fights themselves are well balanced, at least on paper. Enemy abilities are straightforward and well telegraphed, so you can immediately see where the main danger lies. All the bosses have their own unique design, so it never feels like a copy-paste template. However, there's something I personally hate in games and I'm becoming allergic to, "pseudo power" determined by your gear level(item level). It's perfectly fine to have numerical displays so players can tell at a glance whether something is better or not. But the monster scaling? When a monster is just "X" gear levels above you, it suddenly becomes a bullet sponge. The monster has "X" times more health. I'm not a fan of that. It just turns monsters into bigger bullet sponges, and it gets annoying.
TLDR; Great with friends, okay solo. Fine building system, simple builds, good customization, but ruined by gear scaling and repetitive progression. Monsters become bullet sponges, grind gets old fast. Play on private servers with adjusted settings for the best experience.

[h2] Pros: [/h2]
- Chill, atmospheric soundtrack
- Wide range of customization settings
- Simple, clear, and beginner friendly ability system
- Straightforward progression 
- Solid optimization
- Enemy abilities are well telegraphed
- Unique boss fights
- Map diversity

[h2] Cons: [/h2]
- Designed primarily for groups, solo play feels like an afterthought
- Progression is a linear boss checklist style can be annoying for some players
- Poorly designed gear scaling
- Repetitive grind gets old fast
- Limited replayability - the world is static

[h1] Overall rating: 8/10 [/h1]

From a gameplay perspective, the fantasy of playing as a vampire is incredibly well realised in V-Rising. 

I love the way the screen gradually becomes brighter and more exposed when in the sun while a harsh, angry beam of light shines down on the character from the direction of the light, culminating in this awesome, blinding high contrast effect. It turns what would otherwise be a pretty standard lighting system into a high stakes game of figuring out where it is safe to stand. The lighting system is dynamic and moves as the day goes by, which not only has a verisimilitudious quality but also accurately update and checks when the character is exposed. It's an incredibly robust system and one of my favourite mechanics in the game. It goes without saying, but the team that put it together did an incredible job.

The character needs to feed on blood to survive, and the team have built this system in a very clever way. Each living creature has a blood type and a blood quality. The blood type determines what benefits it bestows to the character, while the blood quality determines the quantity and effectiveness of those benefits. This is not something I really payed much mind when I first started out, but as I started to become aware of blood quality and how better quality blood gives better buffs, I started to "get a taste" for it as it were. I became more selective about the blood types I was consuming and going out of my way to find my favourites, like I was a vampire looking for a good feed. 

The game features a buildcrafting system where you can claim territory build your own castle which you can live in and develop technology to improve yourself and furnish your castle. You get to brood around, take prisoners and order minions to do your bidding. It's great and I'm a sucker for this, but I do have a few issues with it, notably when it comes to making castles with multiple levels. If I build a second floor to my castle, but decide I want to move the stairs or swap out the stairs for another version of them, there's no easy way to correct that. I have to remove the entire upper floor, including all of the walls and furniture, and then all of the walls and pillars sorrounding the stairs. This is frustratingly tedious, and means spending minutes removing and replacing pieces just to change one thing.

I've been playing V Rising again after not touching it since the early access days, and the game has changed quite a bit for the better.

The addition of new areas, Dracula, incursions, castle floors, and a much larger progression system gives players plenty to do. The building system feels much better now with multiple levels, though I still wish castles weren't restricted to designated territories.

There are a lot of bosses now—around 67 V Blood bosses—which can feel overwhelming at times. However, each boss has its own mechanics and unlocks, making progression feel meaningful rather than repetitive. The game does a good job of keeping you moving toward the next goal without becoming too easy or boring.

The incursions add another layer of challenge and provide useful rewards, while the expanded progression keeps the game engaging for much longer than it was in early access.

Overall, V Rising has grown into a much larger and more complete experience while still keeping the challenge and gameplay loop that made it fun in the first place.

Stupid pure friction mechanics turn a game that should have been an entertaining hack and slash action survival RPG into an aggravating mess. The day night cycle is just disruptive. It adds nothing. Basically, nobody notices the system in the best case (which begs the question, why even include the system in the first place?).

The thing that makes me never want to play it again is the multiplayer. The bosses are fun to fight, but not when the health and damage dealt and MOBs spawned scale 100% per player. It turns a somewhat tough fight into an impossible grueling battle that can only be finished through cheesing: one player solos the boss to 5% and then the others join in to get kill credit. It's so lame. 

I don't understand why they made these decisions. The game has so much polish otherwise. The artists did truly a phenomenal job. But the systems designers and game balancing seems to have been released completely untested. It's such a shame. It's a truly beautiful game that I never want to play again.

[b]Introduction :[/b]
V Rising, développé par les Suédois de Stunlock Studios, est sorti officiellement en 1.0 en mai 2024 après deux ans d'accès anticipé qui ont fait du jeu un véritable phénomène. C'est un mélange étonnamment réussi entre action-RPG en vue isométrique, survie multijoueur et base building, le tout enrobé d'une thématique vampirique assumée jusque dans les moindres détails. On y incarne un vampire qui se réveille affaibli après des siècles de sommeil et qui doit reconstruire son château, traquer le sang des mortels les plus puissants pour absorber leurs pouvoirs, et survivre à la lumière du jour qui te désintègre littéralement si tu te fais surprendre. Le jeu se joue en solo, en coop privé ou sur serveurs PvP jusqu'à 40 joueurs, et il s'est trouvé une niche absolument méritée entre Diablo et Valheim.

[b]Ce que j'ai aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]🩸 Le concept vampirique est exploité à fond : soleil mortel, aversion pour l'argent et l'ail, miroirs, transformations en loup ou en chauve-souris, c'est l'essence même du mythe respectée jusqu'au bout
[*]⚔️ Les combats en vue iso sont nerveux, exigeants, et chaque boss a un moveset clair à apprendre, on est très proche d'un Diablo couplé à un souls-like
[*]🏰 Le château est un vrai bonheur à construire, les pièces ont des effets concrets sur le craft et la production, on customise son repaire avec passion
[*]🌒 Le cycle jour/nuit a un vrai sens gameplay, on planifie ses sorties en suivant les arbres et les ombres pour ne pas griller au soleil, c'est génial
[*]👥 Le coop en clan transforme l'expérience : on partage le château, on assigne les rôles, on planifie les raids ensemble, c'est extrêmement satisfaisant
[*]🩹 La progression par absorption de sang (chaque type de sang humain ou animal donne des stats différentes) est une mécanique originale qui pousse à varier les victimes
[*]🎨 La direction artistique gothique avec ses tons sombres et ses effets de lumière est vraiment classe, le jeu a un style affirmé qui le distingue immédiatement
[*]🆕 Les mises à jour post-launch sont énormes, Stunlock continue de pousser du contenu gratuit deux ans après et la 1.1 a redéfini la partie survie
[/list]

[b]Ce que j'ai moins aimé :[/b]
[list]
[*]📖 La narration est quasi inexistante, on comprend qu'on est un vampire qui se réveille et basta, l'ambiance fait beaucoup mais on aurait aimé un fil rouge plus marqué
[*]🎮 La caméra fixe en iso peut gêner sur certains combats, notamment quand des éléments du décor masquent l'action, c'est parfois imprécis
[*]🌐 En PvP serveur public, l'expérience peut être brutale, perdre son château à un raid nocturne en pleine déco c'est rude pour les nerfs
[*]⚙️ La courbe d'apprentissage est costaud au début, le jeu te lâche sur la map sans tutoriel détaillé et il faut bouquiner ou regarder des guides
[*]🔄 Le grind de certaines ressources tardives peut s'étirer, surtout en solo où il faut tout faire soi-même
[/list]

[b]Conclusion :[/b]
V Rising est une vraie pépite et probablement l'une des meilleures sorties du studio Stunlock à ce jour. Le mariage action-RPG/survie/base building fonctionne à merveille et la thématique vampirique est traitée avec un sérieux et un respect du mythe qu'on voit rarement. Les combats sont nerveux, le château est un plaisir à monter et à défendre, et le coop en clan offre des dizaines d'heures de fun garanti. Quelques bémols sur la narration absente et une caméra parfois capricieuse, mais à 35h au compteur je n'ai pas tout vu et je suis sûr d'y revenir pour explorer le contenu de la 1.1. Si t'aimes Diablo, Valheim, ou simplement les vampires faits avec amour, c'est un achat les yeux fermés en promo. Et même au prix fort, vu la durée de vie offerte, le ratio est imbattable.

[b]Note :[/b] ★★★★☆

Sometimes, certain games just click for me. They consume my waking thoughts, my dreams and I obsessively play them when fancy takes me. And it doesn't have to be made in the latest Unreal Engine XD engine either. V Rising is one of those games for me. I played the demo recently and I was instantly hooked.

Many spells from different schools to unlock, gems with massive modifiers to those spells, multiple gear sets and options to fit your playstyle, things to build, things to upgrade, easy way to move base to the new biomes and multiple bosses that are fun to fight (some not so fun though).

If I had few minor gripes it would be that you cannot afford to throw things away in this game because it might come up wayyy later in the game as an crafting requirement. But hoarding is standard in any survival-crafting so there's that. Another one would be rescource hunting times but so much of the options can be changed to fit your needs WITHOUT STARTING OVER a la Valheim. You're at that stage where you simply want to focus on killing bosses and progress? Increase resource yield rate to 3x times. You are a massive hoarder but the stack size is too small? Set it to max! The game getting a bit easy and you want to have a challenge? Increase enemy numbers, damage and health and go to town! But make no mistake Brutal difficulty option exists and that changes up bosses to a whole new level. They hit harder, larger health pool and have new moves.

In sum, V Rising is a highly customizable fun survival-crafting game that has so many features that it will keep you busy and engaged for a very long time to come.

Hello everyone,

I bought V Rising about a month ago, and it has completely exceeded all my expectations.

First of all, I want to point out that all DLCs are purely cosmetic. This was actually one of the reasons why I didn’t buy the game earlier. I thought I would be forced into endlessly buying DLCs and that purchasing the base game alone wouldn’t be enough. But the opposite is true — you only need to buy the game, and you have access to all gameplay content.

Now, about the game itself. So far, I honestly have nothing to complain about. The progression is very enjoyable. If you’re tired of games like Diablo or PoE, where countless useless items and weapons keep dropping all the time, that’s not the case here. You might get a weapon drop every now and then — maybe one or two during a couple of hours of gameplay.

I’ve always wanted a game where rewards feel thoughtfully planned rather than completely random. I don’t want to kill a boss and receive an upgrade for a class I’m not even playing. V Rising reminds me of older classics where progression was designed with care.

The building system is great, and I especially like how new features and mechanics are introduced gradually. The game keeps expanding naturally without becoming overwhelming. I really dislike games where you’re expected to learn a thousand new mechanics within the first hour. Fortunately, V Rising is not like that at all.

I don’t want to exaggerate, but I’m genuinely enjoying this game a lot, and I’m very happy that I decided to buy it. (An AI actually explained the DLC system to me, which helped me finally make the decision.)

[hr][/hr][h2] Gameplay [/h2]
Follow the typical survival gameplay loop - gather resources -> build a base and craft items -> but throw in the fun change up of unlocking new crafting recipes, stations and spells from killing the next boss in the progression tree.

All of the bosses in this game are really refreshingly unique, with their own fun attack patterns to deal with, which is surprising as there is a substantial amount. Along with some new and improved versions on the brutal difficulty! [i](Shout out to the granny on brutal!)[/i]

You play on PvP or PvE based on server you play on, with PvP having base raiding mechanics - but I personally feel this game is best enjoyed on private PvE server with friends.

One of the only downsides is tracking your camera on yourself or bosses when constantly dashing around in combat can be quite awkward at times. 
[hr][/hr][h2] Narrative [/h2]
Awaken as a new weak vampire in a world with many regions and bosses to overcome while gathering strength to beat the one and only Dracula.
[hr][/hr][h2] Visuals [/h2]
Lovely gothic fantasy style world.

Different regions have their own unique aesthetics in both the environment and enemies.

All bosses have their own clear design differences, even when their archetype can overlap on ocassion.

Different spell schools have their own easily disguinsible colour scheme making it clear to tell what effect can expect enemies to have on them.
[hr][/hr][h2] Sounds [/h2]
Wonderfully punchy sound effects all around, from the different types of weapons, spells, villagers, creatures and bosses.
[hr][/hr][h2] Linux Support [/h2]
Worked perfectly fine on CachyOS with native proton package.
